name: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd

items.statement: Expects over 25% growth in both top line and bottom line in FY27, continuing thereafter.
items.quote: the company is quite hopeful of achieving reasonable growth of more than 25% in financial year '27 at both the top line and margin level and expected this growth momentum to continue in the subsequent years.

items.statement: Targets minimum 25% growth in top line and bottom line this year.
items.quote: this year, minimum 25% in both top line and bottom line.

items.statement: BESS capex of about INR200 crores for 5 GWh and INR35 crores for container facility.
items.quote: So all practical, you can say INR200 crores is for our BESS capex and INR35 crores is our container facility.

items.statement: Order book entering Q4 FY26 was INR5,369 crores, with INR4,000 crores new and INR1,369 crores legacy.
items.quote: Our consolidated order book entering Q4 2000 financial year stood at INR5,369 crores, comprising around INR4,000 crores of new projects and INR1,369 crores of legacy orders.

items.statement: Targets INR5,000 crores order book annually, with own share INR2,500-3,000 crores.
items.quote: This year also, our target should be the INR5,000 crores, where our orders should be INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores or more than that.

items.statement: New orders taken at minimum 10% margin; overall margin to rise as new order share increases.
items.quote: all the new orders, we are taking minimum 10% margin, if not more. So as soon as our execution in the new order will keep on increasing in the total revenue of that quarter, the margin percentage will keep on increasing.

items.statement: Water and power volumes to reach 50% each by FY30; BESS and power turnover to grow gradually.
items.quote: we are thinking that by 2029-'30, our water and power volume will be 50%. So you will find it gradually move on the BESS turnover and the power turnover going forward along with our water turnover.

items.statement: All new contracts have price variation clauses covering war-related risks.
items.quote: All our new contracts have price variation clause, which covers any risk posed by the war.

items.statement: Raised INR476 crores since May 2024, including promoter contribution of INR313.5 crores.
items.quote: The company has raised INR476 crores since May 2024, of which the total promoter contribution is INR313.5 crores.

items.statement: Plans minimum INR45 crores NARCL repayment in FY27, making FY28 liability negligible.
items.quote: the company further plans to pay a minimum of INR45 crores in the current financial year, which will make the 2027-'28 liability almost negligible.

items.statement: Tax shield from accumulated losses over INR500 crores; no tax payment for a few years.
items.quote: It is more than INR500 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR750-1,000 crores, similar to FY26 spend of INR1,050 crores
items.quote: last year, we incurred about INR1,000 crores. So next year also, the plan would be to incur about INR750 crores to INR1,000 crores on the capital expenditure side.

items.statement: Defense order book stands at over INR1,500 crores with supply schedules of 1-3 years; Switch India EV order book at 1,600 units
items.quote: our order pipeline on defense is strongest ever. So it is already above INR1,500 crores, which are the orders in our hand, which are due for execution and supply.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 14.6%, full year at 13% (up 30 bps YoY); Q1 FY27 faces significant commodity cost pressure, predominantly steel
items.quote: With full year EBITDA margin at 13%, we have now truly entered the teen bracket. This is an improvement of 30 basis points from last year.

items.statement: Price increase of 1% taken effective January 2026, 1-1.5% from April 2026; commodity cost pressure significant in Q1 FY27, mainly steel
items.quote: we have taken a price increase of about 1%, 1.5%, but we'll have to wait and see whether we'll be able to sustain the kind of price increase for the full quarter.

items.statement: CV demand resilient due to GST rationalization and fleet replacement; April-May 2026 positive, fleet owners sticking to 12-18 month expansion plans despite diesel price hikes
items.quote: most of the fleet owners are sticking to their plans for the year in terms of expansion of the fleet. So that is kind of a very good signal as far as the demand is concerned overall on the next 2 to 3 or 4 quarters basis.

items.statement: New HIPPO tractors, TAURUS tippers, 280 HV MAV trucks, 4.1T Bada Dost LCV and Phoenix export LCV launched; market share gains expected in tipper and tractor segments from Q2 FY27
items.quote: you will definitely see this impact starting quarter 2. In quarter 1 also, the dispatches would not be to the full extent of the demand and because there is a certain lead time in ramping up the production of new products.

items.statement: Battery pack manufacturing facility groundbreaking at Pillaipakkam; construction to start in 8-10 weeks, target production start Q2 FY27; phased approach: pack first, then cell manufacturing
items.quote: We should be able to start construction work within the next 8 to 10 weeks, I would suppose. And the target for the start of production would be Q2 of next year.

items.statement: Key risks: commodity price volatility (steel, aluminum, copper, rubber), diesel availability/price hikes, rupee depreciation, transportation and conversion cost inflation
items.quote: there is also a lot of conversion, which happens even on the raw material side where we pay the conversion cost. And finally, we'll also have to look at how this exchange is going to behave.

items.statement: Investments in subsidiaries need-based: HLF, HHF and OHM may require funds; Switch Mobility profitable (PAT ~INR100+ crores) and comfortable; repaid GBP30m of GBP80m Optare loan
items.quote: we will do that based on the requirement. And we have plans, as indicated to you earlier, some of the subsidiary companies like Hinduja Leyland Finance, and its subsidiary Hinduja Housing Finance as well as OHM, these would require funds.

items.statement: FY26 record performance: revenue INR44,007 cr (+13.6%), EBITDA INR5,721 cr, PAT INR3,914 cr; net cash INR5,899 cr (+INR1,650 cr YoY); MHCV market share 30.8%, LCV share 12.7% (+80 bps); exports 18,082 units (+18.5%)
items.quote: FY '26 revenue was at INR44,007 crores, higher by 13.6%. EBITDA for the quarter was at INR2,066 crores and EBITDA margin was at 14.6%. With full year EBITDA margin at 13%, we have now truly entered the teen bracket.

items.statement: Expects acquired group EBITDA of EUR 35 million for FY27
items.quote: We expect to deliver an EBITDA of 35 million for the next financial year.

items.statement: Targets EUR 90-100 million EBITDA for acquired group over next 3-4 years
items.quote: We expect to achieve 90 million to 100 million over the next 3 to 4 years as guided at the time of acquisition.

items.statement: Guides 8-10% revenue growth for Legacy Sudarshan business in FY27
items.quote: Given the geopolitical crisis, we should deliver 8% to 10% of growth this year.

items.statement: No new capex needed for projected growth; sufficient capacity headroom exists
items.quote: Our projection of what EBITDA we've shown in the 3 to 4 years does not require any investment for volumes.

items.statement: Reduced acquired group inventory by EUR 29 million in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We had planned to reduce inventory by 20 million. We've reduced inventory by 29 million

items.statement: Targets further EUR 15-20 million inventory reduction in FY27
items.quote: We hope that we are able to further optimize our inventories to the tune of EUR 15 million to 20 million.

items.statement: Acquired group delivered Business EBITDA of EUR 11 million in Q4 vs EUR 9-10 million guided
items.quote: For the acquired group, we had projected Business EBITDA of Euro 9-10 million, but we delivered, Euro 11 million.

items.statement: Consolidated Business EBITDA for Q4 FY26 was INR 118 crores
items.quote: With this our business EBITDA for the quarter underreporting is INR118 crores.

items.statement: Accelerating value capture to pass on raw material and energy cost increases to customers
items.quote: We further accelerated our value capture efforts and we selected ensuring that we are able to pass on the cost increases to our customers.

items.statement: Energy costs are 6-7% of revenue for acquired group after recent increases
items.quote: So Rajesh ji, this is in the range of 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Q4 volume recovery driven by destocking end and customer restocking, not price hikes
items.quote: Majorly volume growth -- volume-related growth has come in. We have not gone through any price increases, in Q4. This is all volume recovery.

items.statement: Near-term demand muted due to geopolitical crisis; long-term pigment industry growth 3-4% globally
items.quote: The general industry growth of 2 to 3 years is -- generally the pigment industry goes with the GDP of that area and our overall growth of the industry varies between 3% to 4% globally.

items.statement: Middle East crisis causing raw material price increases, supply constraints, and higher logistics costs
items.quote: The Gulf war situation has definitely impacted our cost base and several raw materials used by one Sudarshan are petroleum-derived and we are facing both price increase and supply constraints.

items.statement: Shifted commodity production to Roha, India; Frankfurt site focused on specialties
items.quote: We've already moved some of the commodity products to the Indian Heubach site in Roha and Frankfurt family remains towards speciality coverage.

items.statement: Management expects ~18% volume growth for FY27 across the full product portfolio, driven primarily by frozen foods and Tetra Recart.
items.quote: Considering the present situation and market scenario or information, whatever update we are getting from customers, we are expecting around 18% volume growth for this financial year.

items.statement: Frozen foods volume grew ~28% in FY26 and is expected to continue strong momentum into FY27 with U.S. and Middle East demand.
items.quote: Frozen foods continued its strong momentum, delivering volume growth of approximately 28% during FY26, supported by increasing demand for value-added products and growing interest from the U.S. market.

items.statement: Spray drying capacity expansion of 120 MTPA at INR 2.5 crores; commercial run targeted for December 2025.
items.quote: Commercial run targeted December. And we are trying to see if we can prepone by 2025 base as the target you are asking. But December month, definitely commercial production likely to start.

items.statement: Pectin plant commercially operational; targeting 50% capacity utilization in FY27 yielding INR 7-8 crores revenue at ~70% gross margin.
items.quote: So INR7 - 8 crores of revenue is what we can actually expect at 50% utilization and the gross margins are approximately around 70%-odd of that.

items.statement: Frozen foods segment carries ~50% gross margin but higher cold-chain costs (10x ambient) reduce EBITDA contribution.
items.quote: The frozen food segment actually has around 50% gross margins.

items.statement: Management does not guide EBITDA margin percentages due to cost-plus pass-through model; focuses on per-ton margin improvement.
items.quote: We are expecting on volume growth 17%. But EBITDA, we won't be able to tell you or we generally don't disclose because our model is cost-plus model where we pass through that.

items.statement: Middle East demand disrupted in Q4 FY26 by geopolitical conflict; expected to normalize over time with pent-up post-COVID demand.
items.quote: We expect demand from Middle East to normalize over time.

items.statement: Internal target: non-mango businesses to contribute 40% of revenue in 4-5 years without degrowing mango business.
items.quote: So, the internal strategy over a period of time is to actually make the other businesses contribute 40% of the total revenue without degrowing the mango business.

items.statement: El Niño impact uncertain; raw material availability not a concern but price volatility is the key risk.
items.quote: Challenge is the price. When there is a mismatch in the demand supply, the price moves, I mean, either direction in a very bad way.

items.statement: PLI scheme: INR 83 crores received to date out of INR 145 crores total; INR 60 crores remaining over next 2 years.
items.quote: We've received around INR83-odd crores. The total that we can actually get under the scheme is around INR145 crores. So INR60-odd crores are remaining.

items.statement: Long-term debt ~INR 71-72 crores; annual repayment ~INR 20 crores from internal accruals; no asset sales planned.
items.quote: Our annual commitment is around INR20 crores. So, we'll be comfortable to pay from our internal accrual, not an issue.

items.statement: Targets annual export revenues of up to Rs 1,000 crore by FY27-28.
items.quote: This is underpinned by a medium-term roadmap to FY27-28 where we are targeting annual export revenues of up to Rs 1,000 crore, supported by deeper penetration in Russia and China and re-entry into the European Union and a measured build-out of our domestic and value-added portfolio.

items.statement: Value-added products were 7-10% of export volume; aims to double that share.
items.quote: As far as our export portfolio is considered, value-added products made up roughly 7-10% of overall volume for the year gone by. And if all export factors remain fairly normal in terms of markets and geopolitics, we are hopeful of doubling that contribution in terms of percentage by volume.

items.statement: Anticipates US exports to scale up significantly in FY27 due to tariff reduction.
items.quote: So, all factors considered, we anticipate that our U.S. exports this year will scale up significantly compared to the last couple of years.

items.statement: New PD Curl control product adds 5-10% incremental EBITDA margin over base.
items.quote: So, in this specific scenario we have seen incremental EBITDA margins in excess of 5% up to almost 10% over and above our base EBITDA.

items.statement: Setting up 1 MW solar plant for captive consumption; part commissioned in Q4, balance soon.
items.quote: The company is in the midst of setting up a one-megawatt solar power plant for captive consumption in its processing division. Part of the project has already been commissioned in Q4 and the balance will be commissioned shortly.

items.statement: Passing some raw material costs to contract farming partners; aims to improve export realizations.
items.quote: So, some amount of the costs are being passed on to our channel farming partners but we intend to pass on better realizations to them by ensuring that at the exports level, we generate better contracts with improved margins.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility and erratic weather are key short-term risks.
items.quote: So, in the short term, I think raw material pricing being volatile across the spectrum is a risk for the sector. And weather also being erratic, I think there are certain reports that there could be intense weather during the rest of the calendar year this year.

items.statement: Optimistic on EU demand in FY27 due to India-EU FTA; expects increased exports.
items.quote: We do remain optimistic with respect to European demand being accessible during the course of the current fiscal. The EU-FTA trade has for the most part resulted in a positive sentiment.

items.statement: Penetrated China with black tiger shrimp, added five customers; plans deeper penetration.
items.quote: We also penetrated a new market in the form of China for a new product range altogether, which is black tiger shrimp. In that context, we have worked with five customers so far in the year gone by and intend to penetrate the market deeper during the current fiscal.

items.statement: Commenced sales to Hyperpure in Q4 FY26 for domestic market with raw frozen shrimp.
items.quote: In this context, we are happy to share that the company has commenced sales to Hyperpure in Q4 of FY2025-26 with the initial plan for the domestic market involving selling of base products such as raw frozen shrimp.

items.statement: Market share in Indian shrimp exports is 0.5-0.75%; feed vertical sub 2%.
items.quote: Our market share as far as Indian exports is concerned is currently about 0.5%. Indian exports for shrimp is typically in the region of around 50,000 to 55,000 crores. And we are ranging between 0.5% to 0.75% currently.

items.statement: No new clients added in US in FY26 due to tariff turbulence; optimistic for FY27.
items.quote: With respect to our other export markets, such as the U.S., we did not add any new clientele during the year because there was a lot of turbulence on behalf of the tariffs and certain other factors.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expected to cross INR3,000 crores
items.quote: if you look at, I guess, on an overall basis, we are expecting to cross INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to exceed 10.25% (adjusted FY26 level)
items.quote: we expect that we should see an improvement in the overall margin levels as well going beyond 10.25% that we have achieved last year, if we exclude the onetime impact.

items.statement: Exports to grow 32% in FY27, primarily to Germany and USA
items.quote: the exports will grow by 32% this year, and primarily to Germany and to U.S.A.

items.statement: Railway revenue target INR100 crores in FY27; defense target INR50 crores
items.quote: we should be crossing INR100 crores as far as the railways are concerned. And that's what our internal target is, and we should be able to achieve that. Defense is a little slow, and we are targeting -- we are trying to see how do we cross INR50 crores this year.

items.statement: Hosur facility expected operational from September 2026 for hybrid/EV programs; Tamil Nadu subsidy INR39 crores over 10 years
items.quote: The facility is expected to become operational from September 2026 onwards and will primarily cater to hybrid and EV-related programs for key OEM customers. Along with that, the company has also received an approval from Tamil Nadu government for a subsidy of around INR39 crores, which will start accruing from current

items.statement: FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin 10.25% after excluding INR11 crores Labour Code and INR19 crores lag settlement impacts
items.quote: if you exclude this onetime impact, the margin increases from 9-odd percent to 10.25%.

items.statement: Industry outlook FY27: PV 5-7%, 2W 6-8%, CV 4-6%, 3W 9-10%; 2W EV penetration 7-8%
items.quote: passenger vehicles expected to grow by around 5% to 7%, 2-wheelers by around 6% to 8%, and commercial vehicles by around 4% to 6%, and 3-wheelers by around 9% to 10%. EV penetration in the 2-wheeler segment is also expected to improve further to around 7% to 8%

items.statement: 40 new program launches ramping in FY27, including hybrid/EV components; single-source supplier for many
items.quote: there are almost about 40 launches which are taking place at the moment and all new products, and you'll see the impact coming up in the coming quarters. Actually, end of the third quarter to fourth quarter.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks could disrupt export growth to US and Germany
items.quote: Unless, of course, the global -- the geopolitics which is happening and that brings about some disaster, I think we are ready to reach the levels that we are talking of now.

items.statement: Private Markets recovery target of INR250-300 crores for FY27 maintained
items.quote: we seem to be pretty much on target to be between the INR250 crores and INR300 crores number for FY27

items.statement: Private Markets loan book growth target of 15-20% YoY, targeting INR5,000 crores by March 2027
items.quote: our target is to grow the loan book at 15% to 20% year-on-year

items.statement: Long-term target of 15% revenue growth and 15% ROE at group level
items.quote: two most important things for us will be 15% revenue growth and 15% return on equity at the end of the investment cycle

items.statement: Significant reduction in BlinkX/digital broking investments of INR40-50 crores annually, savings visible in next 3-6 months
items.quote: We are trimming those down. We are cutting those down significantly. You'll hear more about the plans around BlinkX but you will see that number go down significantly over the next 3 to 6 months itself

items.statement: IPO pipeline at INR140,000 crores with 55 IPOs filed, pipeline expected to double to ~INR2 lakh crores by October
items.quote: our pipeline year-on-year from, say, June, July last year to around September, October this year would have almost doubled

items.statement: Equity capital markets slow due to FPI selling and domestic MF conservatism; recovery expected in H2 FY27
items.quote: we are hoping that for this year, the second half will be better than the first half

items.statement: Private Markets shifting to fee-based syndication model; corporate credit growing, real estate lending cautious
items.quote: our business model will evolve to be more fee-based, more fee generative and syndication led

items.statement: Real estate cycle turning; risk-adjusted returns not attractive, slowing real estate lending
items.quote: I'm seeing early signs of slowdown. So it is to build that book back on the corporate side and more diversified

items.statement: Pre-sales target for FY27 is Rs. 2,200 crores, with Senior Living targeted to cross Rs. 700 crores.
items.quote: The pre -sales target for this year is Rs. 2,200 crores that we are targeting. But I would say more importantly, I think we are really looking to grow Senior Living. Senior living is targeted to cross even Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: Expects reported ROE >20% in FY27, with margin improvement.
items.quote: I think we are on track to get to more than 20% reported ROEs for the year.

items.statement: FY27 margin profile better than FY26; FY28 better than FY27.
items.quote: But the margin profile for a full year basis in 2027 will be better than 2026. And the margin profile in FY28 will be better than 2027 overall.

items.statement: Plans to deploy capital in business growth, especially Senior Living, not buybacks/dividends.
items.quote: So, right now the thought is deploy as much as we can in growing the business rather than returning back capital to shareholders either by form of buyback or dividends.

items.statement: Senior Living projects expected 30-35% project-level margins, 35-40% gross margins.
items.quote: I think we can look at about gross profit margins of between 35%-40% and you are looking at about 5-6% of selling cost and therefore about 30%-35% of margins at the project levels on average.

items.statement: Expects 8-10% increase in construction costs in FY27.
items.quote: I think we are expecting about 8-10% increase in construction costs in this financial year, on a year -on-year basis, as of now , given the information we have

items.statement: Signs of oversupply in Gurugram and Pune; no oversupply in Bhiwadi, Jamshedpur, Jaipur.
items.quote: There is no oversupply yet. Signs of some oversupply in Gurugram and Pune are visible.

items.statement: Blended realizations expected to reach ~Rs. 10,000/sq ft as Senior Living grows.
items.quote: I would say maybe, hopefully should move to about 10,000 on a blended basis as Senior Living starts becoming a larger profile.

items.statement: Risks: excess competition, overexpansion, managerial capacity, wrong market choices, approval delays, cost inflation.
items.quote: One, excess competition could come in, but I right now believe this competition should actually grow the market. Second, we might take up more than we can chew. So, Senior Living will grow, but may not grow at the pace that we expect it to grow. Third, we may not be able to handle it managerially in the number of proje

items.statement: Received Rs. 100 crores from IFC via NCDs for Ashiana Aaroham Gurugram.
items.quote: In addition, Ashiana Aaroham Gurugram received funding support from IFC through allotment of Rs. 100 crores of listed unsecured redeemable NCDs.

items.statement: Targets cumulative PAT of Rs. 2,000 crores by FY30; on track.
items.quote: FY30 guidance of Rs. 2000 crore cumulative PAT, what are the biggest bottlenecks to achieving it?

items.statement: Launches planned: Oma in 2 months, Aaranya and Tattvam in Q4 FY27.
items.quote: Ashiana Oma is a premium housing project in Jaipur where all approvals have been received. We should launch in the next couple of months. Ashiana Aaranya and Ashiana Tattvam are slated for launch in the Q4 of this year.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guidance for FY27 including Unichem.
items.quote: So overall company as a whole, we should be able to , including Unichem and put together around 12% to 13% kind of growth on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance for FY27.
items.quote: And on EBITDA side from 20.7% currently on a consolidated basis, I think it shoul d be almost around 22% or 22.3% something more or less on that line.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement guidance for FY27, lower than earlier due to material cost.
items.quote: And therefore, I have given the projections also of guidelines for the EBITDA margin for whole of the year that it should -- it will move by around 1% to 1.25% in the current financial year.

items.statement: Domestic business growth guidance for FY27.
items.quote: Let's say, India should be growing around 12% to 13% in the current financial year.

items.statement: CIS market growth guidance for FY27.
items.quote: CIS market will have around 10% to 11%.

items.statement: Promotional market growth guidance for FY27.
items.quote: Overall promotional ma rket, we expect almost around 12% to 13% kind of growth.

items.statement: Generic market growth guidance for FY27 including U.S.
items.quote: Then overall generic market wil l also have around 12% to 13% kind of growth, which will include the U.S. also.

items.statement: Unichem EBITDA margin guidance for FY27.
items.quote: We foresee that I think Unichem margin may become around 12% to 13% in the current financial year from that level.

items.statement: Plans to take 6-7% price increase in domestic decontrolled products to offset input cost rise.
items.quote: And overall, the other decontrolled products as aga inst 5% kind of price rise, which we are taking. Looking at the overall input cost increase, we -- this year price rise a little higher, may be around 6% to 7% to offset the kind of price increase which has happened at the marketplace.

items.statement: Overall material costs expected to rise 10-12% due to input price increases.
items.quote: And overall, I se e if current end of petroleum prices remain, overall material costs should rise by almost around 10% to 12%.

items.statement: API business passing on entire cost increase to customers.
items.quote: Like say, as far as API is concerned, what we are sellin g today, entire cost increase, we are passing on to the consumer or to the buyers.

items.statement: Plans to launch 6-8 products in U.S. generics in FY27.
items.quote: And I think this year also maybe around 6 to 8 prod ucts will be commercialized in the current financial year.

items.statement: Unichem plans to launch 5-6 products in FY27.
items.quote: Unichem has also a good pipeline, and I think they should also be launching at least 5 to 6 products in the current year.

items.statement: Freight costs up 25% in Q4 and continuing, impacting profitability.
items.quote: So overall, I think our freight cost has moved up by almost, I think, in the fourth quarter by almost around 25%. And that trend is continuing currently also.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR3,400-3,500 crores and PAT of INR700-750 crores.
items.value: INR3,400 crores to INR3,500 crores revenue; INR700 crores to INR750 crores PAT
items.quote: Our expectation is, Rahul, that we should do about INR3,400 crores to INR3,500 crores of revenue. Our PAT expectation is between INR700 crores to INR750 crores.

items.statement: South African associate expected to generate $580-600 million revenue and $47-48 million PAT.
items.value: $580 million to $600 million revenue; $47 million to $48 million PAT
items.quote: our South African associate firm should do, depending on the exchange rate, about $580 million to $600 million of revenue. And the PAT expectation of that is about $47 million to $48 million

items.statement: Earnings to compound 15-25% annually starting FY28, with FY27 as base year.
items.quote: our earnings should compound around 15% to 25% every year starting from '28. So '27 will be a base year where we'll settle around INR700 crores, INR750 crores.

items.statement: PAT to drop by half in FY27 due to no major launches and competitive environment.
items.quote: So it's going to drop by half. So I think we will see a contraction for sure. We're going to drop to about INR700 crores, INR750 crores this year.

items.statement: R&D expenditure expected to be 7-9% of sales next year.
items.quote: In terms of like R&D expenditure next year, I think we expect to spend about 7% to 9%.

items.statement: Semaglutide sales expected to reach INR75-100 crores annualized.
items.quote: I think we are thinking that we should be able to do about INR75 crores to INR100 crores annualized over the year.

items.statement: Brazil subsidiary expected to grow to $55-60 million revenue this year.
items.quote: we are expecting that business should go to INR55 million to INR60 million this year.

items.statement: Canada business expected to grow 10-15% with major launches in FY28-29.
items.quote: Canada, we are expecting will grow around 10% to 15%. It's already a fairly comfortable business. We have a couple of big launches, but that's in '27, '28, not in '26, '27.

items.statement: Input raw material costs increased 25-30% due to West Asia war, may impact later in year.
items.quote: we have already seen 25% to 30% increase in the input raw materials. And see, I think even industry, fortunately, most of the procurement for the kharif, at least half of the procurement has already been done.

items.statement: Net cash of INR2,400 crores available for acquisitions.
items.quote: So net cash would be around INR2,400 crores at a group level.

items.statement: Tax rate under new regime expected around 25% including surcharge.
items.quote: So, including the surcharge, it would be around 25%.

items.statement: U.S. front end business expected to break even this year.
items.quote: U.S., we just bought a front end about a few years ago. Still is losing money. So hopefully, this year, we'll be able to break even.

items.statement: Vizag facility expecting U.S. FDA inspection this year.
items.quote: Vizag is a facility that has not had an inspection, I think nearly, I think I would say, a long time. So we're expecting an inspection sometime this year any moment.

items.statement: Planning 8-9 U.S. filings this year, targeting complex and first-to-file products.
items.quote: Hopefully, this year, we are trying another 8, 9. So trying to target a couple of complex and first to files. Hopefully, we'll have 1 or 2 this year.

items.statement: FY2026 consolidated revenue ~Rs.161.68 Cr, up 67% YoY; PAT ~Rs.12.3 Cr, up 10x YoY; operating cash flow ~Rs.6.1 Cr positive
items.quote: Consolidated revenue increased to approximately Rs.161.8 Crores compared to Rs.96.6 Crores in FY2025, representing growth of nearly 67% year-on-year.

items.statement: Targets 18-20% consolidated EBITDA margin for FY2027-FY2029
items.quote: We are targeting to maintain around 18% to 20% overall, the profitability of EBITDA in the coming years 2026, 2027, and 2028, 2029.

items.statement: Estimates ~Rs.50 Cr capex for future expansions, still evaluating alternatives
items.quote: As we look ahead, management estimates around 50 crore capital could be required to support future expansions, however the management is still evaluating its alternatives as of now.

items.statement: Hospital segment at ~70% gross profit and 15% operating profit; aims to reach peer EBITDA levels of ~20%
items.quote: In the hospital segment, we have around 70% of our GP and 15% of our overall operating profit, but as we compare the other hospitals, listed hospitals, we can find around 20% of the EBITDA we can find with other hospitals.

items.statement: Healthcare currently 22% of revenue; long-term target 70-80% contribution to revenue and profitability
items.quote: Healthcare currently contributes approximately 22% of consolidated revenue, but its strategic significance extends far beyond its current revenue share.

items.statement: Sees growth opportunities in existing facilities (utilization below potential), additional clinics, specialty expansion, international patients, and selective acquisitions
items.quote: Looking ahead, we continue to see opportunities across existing healthcare facilities where utilization remains below the long-term potential. We also see opportunities through additional clinics, expansion of specialty services, international patient growth, and selective acquisitions.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased with healthcare scaling; TPA/institutional settlement cycles affect collections; improving working capital efficiency is key focus
items.quote: Trade receivable increased during the year as healthcare platform continued to scale, while healthcare receivables are naturally influenced by TPA and institutional settlement cycles. Improving collections and working capital efficiency remains key focus areas going forward.

items.statement: Committed to strong balance sheet, positive cash flow, low leverage; will deploy capital prudently for organic expansion, capacity optimization, partnerships, selective acquisitions
items.quote: We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet, positive cash flow, and low leverage provide us with flexibility, but we intend to deploy capital very prudently.

items.statement: FY2026 first year with full operating platform visible in reported numbers; positive operating cash flow of Rs.6.1 Cr validates earnings quality
items.quote: FY2026 represented the first year where the full operating platform was visible in reported numbers.

items.statement: Medium to long-term conductor EBITDA margin guidance of INR35,000-36,000 per metric ton plus tailwinds
items.quote: based on the historical EBITDA margin that we have made, we expect that from a medium to long-term perspective, our conductor margins could be in the range of INR35,000 to INR36,000 per metric ton

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR1,500 crores vs INR740 crores in FY26
items.quote: We plan to increase our capex for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores in addition to the FY26 capex that we have incurred of INR740 crores

items.statement: FY27 capex breakup: Conductor INR400 cr, Oil INR200 cr, Cable INR850 cr
items.quote: Around INR400 crores would be coming from conductor division, around INR200-odd crores on oil division, and cable would be in the range of INR850 crores

items.statement: Conductor order book at INR7,671 crores as of March 31, FY26
items.quote: The order book as on March 31 stands at a healthy INR7,671 crores

items.statement: Cable division pending order book at approximately INR1,800 crores
items.quote: The pending order remains at approximately INR1,800 crores

items.statement: FY26 Conductor EBITDA margin INR43,012 per metric ton vs INR36,683 in FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA margin post forex came in at INR43,012 per metric ton compared to INR36,683 per metric ton a year ago

items.statement: FY26 Cable EBITDA margin 10.2% vs 10.6% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA post forex grew by 27.1% to INR633 crores at a margin of 10.2%

items.statement: Aluminum premium (MJP) increased, freight costs up, LME-SHFE spread $330-360/ton
items.quote: There is a fairly large difference between LME and the Shanghai Metal Exchange, what we call the SHFE prices which, for aluminum, has increased to about $330 to $360 a ton

items.statement: Conductor volume growth target 10% YoY, Cable volume growth target 25% YoY
items.quote: Overall figures, we are continuing to look at a 10% growth year-on-year on our Conductor side by volume. We are looking -- continuing to look at growing by 25% a year in our cable side

items.statement: Premium conductor mix 45.8% of FY26 revenue, order book premium mix >50%
items.quote: 45.8% is the mix that we had of premium products. And if you look at that as a percentage of the current order book, it's a little over 50%

items.statement: Middle East war disrupting supply chains, freight, refinery operations, project deferrals
items.quote: The Middle East is where the maximum amount of problems are there because the containers are being transferred without complete insurance cover, resulting in some of the projects being actually deferred or delayed

items.statement: CTC conductor export approvals: Middle East secured, Europe and US in progress
items.quote: Initially, we have got approvals from Middle East manufacturers and has started exporting to them. We are now working towards getting approvals in Europe and the United States as well

items.statement: Plans to increase royalty rate 10-15% annually alongside ~10% volume growth.
items.quote: Yes. Going forward, we are also planning to increase 10% to 15% every year along with a volume growth of around 10%, which we are achieving from last 2, 3 years.

items.statement: Own manufacturing plant to continue 100% capacity utilization in near future.
items.quote: This year, we have utilized 100%, and it will continue to have 100% utilization in the near future also.

items.statement: Royalty charged per ton, so steel price fluctuation does not impact business.
items.quote: We are charging royalty on per ton basis, not on the percentage basis. So the price fluctuation is not impacting our business at all, either in own manufacturing or in the branding business.

items.statement: Royalty rate rose to INR435/ton in FY26 from INR398 last year.
items.quote: Yes. This year, the average rate is INR435 per metric ton which was INR398 last year.

items.statement: Royalty income expected to contribute increasingly larger share of overall earnings.
items.quote: This royalty led revenue model is in our view, the defining financial characteristic of Kamdhenu's business, and we expect it to contribute an increasingly larger proportion of our overall earnings over the coming years.

items.statement: Expects steel demand trajectory to sustain and potentially accelerate over medium term.
items.quote: We expect this demand trajectory to sustain and potentially accelerate over the medium term, driven by a confluence of structural factors.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions in crude oil and gas may pressure near-term margins.
items.quote: While these factors may exert near -term pressure on margins, both for us and for our franchisee partners, the resilience of the underlying demand environment provides confidence in the ability to manage through this period.

items.statement: Framing treasury policy to reward shareholders; no further investment planned in paint business.
items.quote: The treasury will be utilized only for the steel business and reward to the shareholders.

items.statement: Plans to increase market share in South; rest of India focus on existing unit capacity.
items.quote: Yes. In the South, we are planning to add more franchisees. And the rest of India, we are planning to increase the capacity of existing units.

items.statement: Brand premium across India around INR2,600 per ton, up to INR6,000 in some states.
items.quote: Today, in all over India, our premium is around INR2,600 per ton. In some states, our goods are sold for INR6,000 per ton extra, which is the best local brand there.

items.statement: Franchisee capacity around 5 million tons; new data to be released in Q1.
items.quote: And hopefully, in the Q1, we will release this data, the existing capacity is around 5 million.

items.statement: Regional volume mix: North 31%, East 35%, West 19%, South 15%.
items.quote: in North, we have 31%, East, we have 35%, West we have 19%, and South, we have 15% on the overall volume.

items.statement: Estimated retail branded TMT market share around 20%.
items.quote: Ma'am, exact data is not available for the TMT product, but on the estimated basis, we are calculating retail branded market share is 20% of Kamdhenu brand product, retail branded.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 15.6% from 8.58% in Q3 FY26 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25, driven by price pass-through and operational efficiencies.
items.quote: The EBITDA margin as well expanded to 15.6% in Q4 FY26 compared to 8.58% in Q3 FY26 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25, once again representing an expansion of 407 basis points year-on-year and 702 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: Management targets AZO EBITDA margin of ~13% and API EBITDA margin of 15-16% at steady state, significantly above current levels.
items.quote: For both answering on EBITDAs for both the ATC as well as Atlas business, we would guide that Management would like to target EBITDA margin of about 13% of the AZO business. And eventually, if we get the API business right, 15% to 16% in the API business going forward.

items.statement: AZO capacity expansion of ~1.5x planned at Rs. 10-15 crore capex once utilization hits 75-85%, to be funded via internal accruals.
items.quote: As soon as we hit that range, we would like to do a little expansion with a small CAPEX of about Rs. 10 crores to Rs. 15 crores which would probably be financed through internal accruals and increase our capacity.

items.statement: US demand for Blue and AZO pigments reviving after tariff reductions; Europe remains structurally slow but opportunities pursued.
items.quote: We have seen a revival in that. So, our US business, once the tariff has been reduced again, it has again started to improve.

items.statement: Blue pigment margin improvement driven by raw material price pass-through, inventory gains, and operational efficiencies; management aims to sustain higher gross margins.
items.quote: It is a mixture of several factors of internal strategy, a little bit of the inventory addition as well as your operational efficiencies all put together that have driven the strong numbers.

items.statement: Company aims to reach Rs. 1,000 crore revenue within next few years; debt reduction ahead of schedule with strong cash flows across all four units.
items.quote: We will certainly be looking to grow, and we certainly have the goal of reaching Rs. 1000 crore as a company within the next few years.

items.statement: Gokul Jaykrishna stepped down as CEO after 8 years, remains Managing Director; Arjun Jaykrishna appointed CEO to drive next growth phase.
items.quote: As of the last Board meeting, I stepped down as the CEO of Asahi Songwon Colors Limited, and it's been an amazing journey of eight years as a CEO and 17 years as Managing Director.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margins expected to be maintained at Q4 FY26 levels across all three segments
items.quote: on the EBITDA, all three segments should be able to maintain quite easily even under the current circumstances of disruption globally, the margins that we have seen in Q4. So, Q1 should be able to easily maintain those in terms of our performance.

items.statement: No capacity expansion CAPEX planned for Blue business
items.quote: Management view on the capacity and volume growth of the Blue business is clear that we are not looking to do on the Blue business any CAPEXs to increase capacity. This is clear.

items.statement: Chinese API/pigment prices up 30-40% due to export incentive removal, freight doubling, crude rise
items.quote: Chinese has increased around 30% to 40% of their price because of all three reasons.

items.statement: Blue demand environment remains depressed, one of longest low periods since inception
items.quote: probably one of the longest low or depression sustained periods in terms of demand in the chemical industry in general also in Pigments that has been seen since our company started probably.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: Yes, so Yes, the capex for FY27 most likely would be in the range from INR40 crores to INR50 crores and for FY28 another would be in between INR35 crores to INR40 crores.

items.statement: Normalized margins expected in about two years due to delays.
items.quote: So, honestly if you tell me, put my finger on it, it's probably two years away because even '27 we don't see, even so, even if today we say okay to the machinery, it's eight months for it to come and commissioning and, six-eight months for getting things done and established, which requires time and customer approval,

items.statement: Value-added products command ~25% higher margins over extrusion.
items.quote: Our focus has always been now that we've added extrusion capacity, we are adding capacities for our value-added products. That means anodizing, powder coating, machining, and tubing, which is the new business, which command very significant margins of close to 25% over and above the extrusion margins.

items.statement: Aluminium price increases passed through; operating cost pass-through being discussed but not immediate.
items.quote: Yes, of course, we are a converter only. So basically, we pass on the higher increased whatever the in terms of aluminium prices are increased. But yes, the operating cost we are not able to pass on an immediate basis though we have started discussing with the customers and trying to pass on that cost as well. But to a

items.statement: US tariffs and high aluminium prices have slowed exports; 80-85% of exports go to US.
items.quote: So, again, the problem is twofold. The tariff on global, so our big part of our market is the -- is America, right? Out of 100% of our export, about 80%-85% goes to the States. So, that's the largest chunk. That's where we're most impacted.

items.statement: Domestic demand good, especially defense; export demand weak due to US tariffs.
items.quote: But we are also focused on domestic because domestic growth story, especially on the defense side, no, we are seeing a lot of inquiries, and hopefully, we are quite hopeful that we should be able to convert at least few of them, if not all.

items.statement: Aims to sell 100% of extrusion as value-added; 15-20% YoY ramp-up to reach 80% capacity in three years.
items.quote: So, we would ideally in an ideal scenario, if I tell you, I would want to sell 100% of my extrusion, about the 24,000 tons that we are planning to achieve in the next three years, as value-added product. But I mean, the ramp-up is not going to be that significant. But even if we are able to capture the market on 15%-20

items.statement: Dewas precision tube project delayed; renegotiating machinery; target 40-50% utilization in 1-2 years.
items.quote: But the good part is that this is a complete import substitute business. You know, not if not this year or the next year, we are very confident that we should be able to at least do 40-50% of the utilization of that plant. And, that should give us substantial revenue.

items.statement: Ramp-up cost of INR7-10 crores and additional INR10 crores in FY27 for depreciation, finance, employee costs.
items.quote: So, Yes, since again the FY27 would be a investment and commissioning year where our ramp-up cost will, I think will add up to again by INR7 crores INR10 crores in FY27 this year as well unless and until we obtain that operating kind of leverage. This additional cost in form of depreciation, finance cost, and another e

items.statement: No fixed supply contracts; open-ended with no fixed commitments.
items.quote: No, so we don't have any contracts, any fixed return contracts. We generally have non-disclosure agreements in place where we have design and confidential information related clauses in our contract. But there is no fixed commitment contracts of supply or delivery. It's generally very open-ended and it changes dependin

items.statement: Export revenue was ~50% of manufacturing revenue at INR150 crores; diversifying to CIS markets.
items.quote: Yes, so it from export it was almost 50%, about INR150 crores.

items.statement: Expects U.S. D2C revenues to organically grow 35-40% to INR375 crores by end of FY27.
items.quote: Based on current momentum and market tailwinds, we expect our U.S. direct -to-consumer revenues to organically grow between 35% to 40% this year to INR375 crores by end of FY '27.

items.statement: Expects strong profitability growth of 20-30% in the coming year.
items.quote: We expect strong growth in profitability in the coming year in the range of 20% to 30%, supported by our increasing contribution from our direct-to-consumer segment and improving efficiencies.

items.statement: Aims to build a INR1,000 crores direct-to-consumer brand by FY29.
items.quote: Our ambition is to build a INR1,000 crores direct-to-consumer brand by FY29, supported by continued expansion of Jean Dousset and growth across our various other brands, enhance digital capabilities and selective acquisitions that align with our long -term vision.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% annual profitability growth over the next 2-3 years.
items.quote: Our goal is to increase profitability by 25% to 30% each year for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Expects to reach zero net debt in the next 12 to 24 months.
items.quote: As I said, sir, the current priority is to continue to grow the company and become zero net debt, which we expect in the next 12 to 24 months, we will get there.

items.statement: Plans to open 4 additional Jean Dousset stores in FY27, reaching 6 locations.
items.quote: And the plan really is to open 4 stores in the current year in 4 major metropolitan areas. So at the end of FY27, we should be at 6 locations.

items.statement: Each existing Jean Dousset store generates INR30-35 crores annual sales and INR8-10 crores bottom line.
items.quote: Each existing Jean Dousset store generates between INR30 crores and INR35 crores in annual sales depending on the location, demonstrating the strong scalability and revenue potential of the brand's retail model.

items.statement: D2C business EBITDA margins are 15% to 20%.
items.quote: We've outlined the plan to grow our direct-to-consumer business to about INR1,000 crores. And as I've mentioned that the EBITDA margins on that are 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Sees 30-40% organic growth in Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry D2C channel.
items.quote: The website is called Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry and because of this focus, we've been seeing a 30% to 40% organic growth in this channel.

items.statement: No dividend for current year; will consider once zero net debt is achieved.
items.quote: Yeah, for the current year, we've decided not to distribute a dividend because I think the current priority is investing in the growth of the business.

items.statement: Net debt currently around INR200-250 crores; total debt INR450 crores with INR200 crores cash/investments.
items.quote: So as of right now, we have around INR200 crores to INR250 crores of net debt. Our expectation would be that over the next 2 years or so, we should be at a zero net debt position.

items.statement: Currency exposure largely hedged via USD purchases and forward contracts.
items.quote: So at any given point of time, we are more or less completely hedged as far as exposure to currency markets is concerned.

items.statement: May consider share buyback once zero net debt achieved, subject to Board approval.
items.quote: And obviously, based on capital allocation and when we get to zero net debt, the company may buy back shares of the company as well. But these are not decisions that I can take without the Board's consent.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR4,675 crore entering FY27, providing healthy revenue visibility
items.quote: We enter FY27 with an order book of INR4,675 crore, providing healthy revenue visibility and reaffirming customer confidence in our capabilities and execution.

items.statement: Targets INR10,000 crore revenue by 2030 with minimum 15% EBITDA margins
items.quote: And as I mentioned, long term, by 2030, we expect the company to be at about INR10,000 crore of revenue with at least minimum 15% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Odisha Greenfield wheelset project: partial production by end FY27, full commissioning by end FY28
items.quote: Partial production is expected by end of the current financial year, with full commissioning targeted by end of FY28.

items.statement: BESS business targets INR1,000 crore revenue in 3-4 years; added 110 MW BESS orders from Chalukya Power and Pickrenew Energy for FY27
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aspire to build a INR1,000 crore revenue business in batteries and energy storage over the next 3 to 4 years, supported by a growing order pipeline and favourable industry dynamics.

items.statement: Railwheel factory EBITDA margin improved to 17% in FY26 from 12% in FY25; revenue grew from INR343 crore to INR528 crore
items.quote: We achieved 17% EBITDA margins as compared to 12% last financial year. Even in terms of revenue, the revenues have substantially increased from INR343 crore to INR528 crore.

items.statement: Corten steel available domestically but pricing not competitive vs China; PLI scheme expected to bridge 8-10% cost gap for marine containers
items.quote: The challenge is in respect to the pricing compared to China, pricing in India is not sustainable for large-scale production to match the international prices. So definitely, that is where we are looking at the PLI scheme to bridge the gap.

items.statement: Signed long-term wheelset supply arrangement with Tatravagonka (Europe) for export from Odisha facility; validates manufacturing capabilities
items.quote: We also signed a long-term supply arrangement with Tatravagonka, one of Europe's leading wagon manufacturers under which we will supply wheelsets for their requirements from our upcoming Odisha facility.

items.statement: Expects to maintain 50% growth momentum for next five years
items.quote: Our effort is and intention and expectation is for the next five years, given the current scale we are in, for the next five years, we hope that we will maintain the same kind of momentum.

items.statement: Order book of INR1600 crores as of March 2026, 4.46x FY26 revenue
items.quote: The company ended financial year 2026 with an order book of INR1600 crores, equivalent to 4.46x of our financial year 2026 revenue, providing strong visibility for sustained growth in the near to medium term.

items.statement: 60% of INR1600 crore order book executable in FY27, 40% spills to FY28
items.quote: So, approximately we have a balance order book of INR1600 crores, out of which we expect in the coming year, 60% approximately of this balance order book should be executed in the coming year. 40% of it will be spilled over into the next year.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline of INR3000 crores with results expected in 30-45 days; INR7000-8000 crores for full year
items.quote: Currently, we have a bidding pipeline of about INR3000 crores, for which we're expecting the results to come in the next about 30 to 45 days. And in the coming year as a whole, I can say, we will have about INR7000 crores to INR8000 crores in the bidding pipeline, in the entire year.

items.statement: EPC segment margins vary 13-20%, average ~15%; real estate segment at 85% margins
items.quote: So, they all vary between 13% to 20%. So, certain niche works, we get 18%, 19%. The general infrastructure works, 11%, 12%, 13%. So, the average we get about 15% in the EPC sector.

items.statement: Real estate segment contributes ~85% margins, purely rental yield
items.quote: The real estate segment itself has about 85% margins. So, it's purely, almost purely rental income.

items.statement: Order book diversified: Roads & Bridges INR498 cr, Buildings INR405 cr, Railways & Tunnels INR400 cr, River Protection INR250 cr
items.quote: Our divides of order book into the main four parts: Buildings INR405 crores, Roads and Bridges INR498 crores, Railways and Tunnels INR400 crores and River Protection Work INR250 crores.

items.statement: Pipeline mix: ~40% buildings, 20% protection works, 40% roads
items.quote: Pipeline, I'll have to see the numbers, I don't have it in hand. But you can say that about 40% of the works would be building-related works, 20% would be protection-related works, and then 40% would be road works.

items.statement: New retail/commercial project in Guwahati worth ~INR500 crores over 4-5 years, 4 lakh sq ft leasable area
items.quote: In the coming year, we are planning another retail destination, a mix of commercial and residential in Guwahati itself, in the format of an open plaza shopping destination. And this project will be built phase-wise with the approx. total value accumulated to about INR500 crores in the next four to five years, phase-wis

items.statement: Strong Northeast infrastructure outlook: highways, hydropower, border infra, railways, institutional buildings over next 10 years
items.quote: Some segments that are expected to experience very, very good growth is highway infrastructure across the Northeast, hydropower, hydropower projects in Arunachal Pradesh, border infrastructure.

items.statement: Promoter pledge from 2014; working with lenders for release over next 1-2 years as debt reduces
items.quote: Well, the shares have been pledged in 2014, and in the regular consortium meetings, we have a word with our lenders to release the same. And we are working on that, and we hope so in next year or two, we get released all the pledge because earlier there was a higher debt in the company.

items.statement: Capital allocation via surety bonds, bank guarantees, and JV partnerships to support project execution
items.quote: So, we are -- we have applied and also received -- surety bonds are now accepted across all departments. So, with surety bonds -- with the mix of surety bonds and bank guarantees, we expect to support the required cash flows for these new projects. Also, we have a strategic model wherein we have joint ventures with oth

items.statement: ~70% of order book revenue to BIL, ~30% to JV partners; varies by project
items.quote: So, depends on the ratio in which the project we had bid for. So, it is not a standard number across the system, it's project to project. So, approximately you could say 70% of the order book revenues will come into BIL and the 30% will go into our joint venture partners.

items.statement: Expects Q1 FY27 capacity growth of 3-4% year-on-year.
items.quote: we are expecting to add capacity of around 3 -4 percent in Q1FY27 as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Estimates mid-teens improvement in unit passenger revenue in Q1 FY27 vs Q1 FY26.
items.quote: we currently estimate a mid -teens improvement in unit passenger revenue in Q1FY27 vs Q1FY26, primarily driven by the calibrated fuel charge s which has been imposed, and a lower base during the same period last year

items.statement: CASK ex fuel ex forex expected to rise mid- to high single digits.
items.quote: we foresee that it's going to be in mid- to high single digits is what our anticipation is right now.

items.statement: Fares being raised to offset costs; demand currently inelastic to hikes.
items.quote: we need to take fares up to protect ourselves against some of these additional costs that are showing up. And for the moment, what we are discovering is that the fares are sticking.

items.statement: Q1 mix skewed more toward domestic; international Middle East capacity ramping back.
items.quote: given Q1 is a more domestic heavy kind of a play given the seasonality, the ratio is going to be more skewed on the higher side towards domestic and less on the international

items.statement: Middle East conflict disrupted ~18% of capacity and ~160 daily flights.
items.quote: Together, these markets represent around 18 percent of our total capacity and approximately 160 daily flights, and this weighed on utilization and revenues towards the end of the quarter.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation drove large forex losses; sensitivity ~INR900 crore per rupee.
items.quote: anything on the balance sheet, we've got a $1 movement or INR1 movement to dollar tends to translate into INR900 crores.

items.statement: Prepaying USD450mn finance lease obligations to GIFT City entity for aircraft/engine acquisition.
items.quote: we are also prepaying some of our finance lease obligations towards our gift city entity aggregating USD 450mn (43.4 bn rupees), such funds will be utilized towards acquisition of aircraft and engines through our gift city entity.

items.statement: Will deploy cash above 20-25% of revenue safety net toward aircraft ownership.
items.quote: anything above that, we'll start d eploying towards acquisition of assets, which otherwise would have a much higher money cost to pay than what we will get as returns on those from the banks or the mutual funds that we have.

items.statement: No dividend recommended for FY2026.
items.quote: given the financial performance for the year and position of distributable reserves we have decided not to recommend a dividend for FY2026.

items.statement: Pratt & Whitney AOG groundings in 40s, expected to trend down to 30s by year-end.
items.quote: our Pratt and Whitney-related groundings are currently in the 40s and are expected to trend down wards by the end of the year in the 30’s.

items.statement: Returning damp-leased and older aircraft; no change to orderbook deliveries.
items.quote: There is no shift as far as deliveries are concerned related to our order book. But our first attempt is going to be to address it both in a manner of returning the damp leases and then looking at if there are any kind of older technology aircraft that may not need to be utilized as much.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth guidance of 10-11% and revenue growth of 15%+ with price hikes
items.quote: So again, it is very hard to say after that. But again, for FY 27, we are for sure like 15% in revenue growth, I'm saying and volume is 10%, 11%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin improvement target of 100-150 bps with double-digit revenue growth
items.quote: So FY 27 Again, we have an intention to be increased at least 100 basis points to 150 basis points on that with a revenue growth of double digit plus.

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR 67 cr; revised 5-year capex plan from INR 500 cr to INR 400 cr (FY23-27), INR 270 cr spent in first 4 years, INR 130 cr planned for FY27
items.quote: This year the company incurred capital expenditure of INR 67 crores, primarily towards branch expansion, construction of sorting center and technology enhancement initiative across business verticals.
