items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, West Asia conflict, elevated ATF prices (+50%), labor cost increase (~100 bps impact), SIR-related disruptions, airline consolidation
items.quote: While geopolitical uncertainties and elevated fuel prices, may continue to create near-term challenges for the logistics industries. The company remains focused on operational efficiency, service reliability and customer-centric execution.

items.statement: Branch expansion: 100 branches planned in FY27 (40 surface, 60 rail/air/C2C); 70 branches added in FY26
items.quote: So again, in this year, 40 branch would be open for surface business and 60 branches for the rail and air and C2C put together. So again, expansion plan for the 100 branches would be there in this year.

items.statement: SME revenue mix 48-52% (target 50-50); strong traction in pharma, automotive, defense, solar, EV, e-commerce D2C brands
items.quote: Since last two decades, we maintaining in a 50-50 right now is around 48 to 52 because again, everyone knows SMEs are under stress slightly. And that's why this ratio is, but we are trying hard to be getting back into 50% plus, obviously.

items.statement: Target to double RTD business in FY27 to cross 200,000 cases from 100,000 cases in FY26
items.quote: our expectation is that in the year 2, which is FY27, we will double this business to cross 200,000 cases.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to settle in 76-80% range as RTD mix (70% GM) grows; EBITDA margin target ~20% via operating leverage
items.quote: I believe our overall gross margins will be between 76% to 80%.

items.statement: Export revenue doubled in FY26; targeting 5% of total revenue from exports from FY27 onwards; international footprint expanded to 15 countries
items.quote: We expect 5% of total revenue to come from exports from FY '27 onwards.

items.statement: Discounts/schemes flat for 2-3 years; no price hikes mentioned; cost structure geared for doubling business without major changes
items.quote: Our schemes and discounts, as we call them, have remained fairly consistent year-on-year over the last 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: CSD channel contributes ~8% of revenue with 45% market share; new approvals for Merlot, Noi Sparkling (H1 FY27) and Shotgun (H2 FY27) to drive growth
items.quote: It already contributes about 8% of our overall revenues, and I see this number only growing going forward.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 18-20% by FY28 at 85% capacity utilization
items.quote: See, at a better capacity utilization of around 85% and good product mix with few high margins part coming into the kitty, we expect to stabilize at EBITDA of around 18 to 20%. Maybe by not maintaining by not FY27, but by FY28 will be at 18% to 20% EBITDA level.

items.statement: Commissioned fourth manufacturing facility in Jaipur with 35,000+ sq ft machining capacity from Jan 1, 2026
items.quote: Commercial product operations commence from January 1, 2026 and the facility adds more than 35,000 sq. ft. of machining capacity.

items.statement: Expects ₹12-14 crore revenue from Jaipur Plant-4 in FY27
items.quote: And coming to revenue expectation, we are expecting the revenue close to around ₹12 crores to ₹14 crores in this financial year from the Plant-4 facility in Jaipur.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 13.3% in FY26 from 10.5% in FY25
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA grew by 63.7% to ₹1244 lakhs with EBITDA margins improving significantly from 10.5% to 13.3%.

items.statement: Tractor sector showing consistent domestic growth plus new growth in European and American agriculture markets
items.quote: In tractor industry, last three years, we have seen a consistent growth of numbers in domestic market. And from this year onwards, the European and American market has started growing, specifically in agriculture sector.

items.statement: EV component revenue contribution at 5.3% in FY26 from Kalyani Techno Forge, Dana Group and Eka Mobility
items.quote: Overall, in FY26, the contribution for EV components were around 5.3% in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Defense sector penetration will take 4-6 quarters to achieve substantial hold due to tendering process
items.quote: However, my experience in this segment is a bit slow so to penetrate and to have a substantial hold on that, it will take another 4-6 quarters at least.

items.statement: Exclusive agreement with Jaipur facility's previous owner for 100% of their machining business
items.quote: The customer whose plant, whose machining setup we have taken it, he will be our customer, he will be our only customer and we will be working for them. So, we have an exclusive agreement where their business, 100% machining business will be routed through Kranti.

items.statement: Crossed ₹100 crore consolidated revenue milestone for first time in FY26 with 28% growth
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenue increased by 28% to crossing ₹100 crores milestone for the first time.

items.statement: Entered defence manufacturing sector through machining orders from AVNL
items.quote: One of the most significant developments during the year was our entry into the defence manufacturing sector through machining orders which we received from AVNL.

items.statement: Not planning immediate acquisitions but inorganic expansion remains in Vision 2030 roadmap
items.quote: Yes, we are not currently planning immediate future. But yes, this is in our roadmap of 2030 where we have to expand organically as well as inorganically.

items.statement: E-commerce business targeted to maintain double-digit growth going forward, described as incremental not high growth.
items.quote: It would not be fair to put a number to it, but the attempt shall be to maintain a double-digit growth if possible.

items.statement: Organic e-commerce business to aim for double-digit growth; new verticals would be additional on top.
items.quote: We are talking about organic business, that is obviously the e-commerce business. And putting a number forward would be speculative, so I would not like to do that at this point.

items.statement: EPR certificate trading platform ready, integrated, awaiting government go-ahead; revenue assessment after 5-6 months of operation.
items.quote: As I said, it is complete, it is ready, it is integrated, it is waiting for the go-ahead to operationalize. And over the first five or six months, we should be able to then be able to assess what would be the revenue streams from these platforms.

items.statement: Travel portal MSTC Smart Travel in final testing, to launch in B2B segment shortly.
items.quote: This portal is also in its final stages of testing, and we expect to operationalize it shortly in the B2B space to begin with, and then extend segmental reach as we gain traction.

items.statement: Exiting marketing and trading business; income to be out of business basket by first quarter of this year.
items.quote: So we have decided to exit, and by the first quarter of this year it will be out of our business basket. Already out, but income will be out of our business basket.

items.statement: EBITDA percentage maintained at similar level year-on-year despite competition and macro uncertainty.
items.quote: With respect to the financials, we have been able to maintain EBITDA percentage at a similar level year-on-year.

items.statement: New coal exchange development at very initial stage; coal is significant revenue stream, impact being watched.
items.quote: So this is something at the very, very initial stages and we shall be watching these developments closely to see how they impact our revenue stream going on. Coal does form a significant part of our revenue stream.

items.statement: ELV scrappage flow dependent on state policy framework and incentives; MSTC not primary driver.
items.quote: So as far as the arising and feed of vehicles is concerned, this would be dependent on the policy framework and the incentives that are put into place by the government in a federal structure through various states and so on, based on the guidelines that have been issued by MoRTH.

items.statement: EPR policy for manufacturers driving ELV scrappage traction; expects substantial increase formalizing grey market scrapping.
items.quote: So a bit of the traction which is happening for the increase is being driven by the OEMs. And we expect that to naturally substantially increase, which would help to basically formalize the scrapping which is happening mainly today through the grey market.

items.statement: EPR platform revenue will be transaction fee-based, adding to top line and bottom line.
items.quote: No, it will be based on the fee basis. We will have some front kind of fee on the transaction. So that will be part of our top line and of course that will be our revenue.

items.statement: Opened corporate office in New Delhi; overheads increased, expected to translate into revenue in near future.
items.quote: There are some increases in the overheads because this year we have opened a corporate office at New Delhi.

items.statement: Targets AUM of ~₹2,500 crore and PAT of ₹80-90 crore for FY2026-27, implying ~3x PAT growth
items.quote: our minimum target for FY2026-27 is approximately ₹2,500 crore of AUM and ₹80 to 90 crores of profitability at the PAT level

items.statement: Targets Mediclaim Financing AUM of ₹1,000 crore (50-60% of total AUM) in FY2026-27
items.quote: we are targeting approximately 50 to 60% of our total AUM to be in Mediclaim Insurance Premium Financing

items.statement: Targets GNPA below 1.5% in FY2026-27 driven by shift to digital financing (60-70% of portfolio)
items.quote: Gross NPA will reduce further to below 1.5% in FY2026-27

items.statement: Long-term target of ₹500 crore+ PAT over next 3-4 years
items.quote: the target over the next three to four years is to reach a profitability of ₹500 crore-plus

items.statement: Weighted average ROA was 2.31% in FY2025-26; targets 10-11% ROA over medium term
items.quote: Our ROA on a weighted average basis for FY2025-26 was 2.31%. We are on a path toward 10 to 11% ROA over the medium term

items.statement: Mediclaim Financing ROA >7-8%; Salary Saathi 4-5%; EV/Solar 2-2.5%
items.quote: Looking at Return on Assets by product: EV and Solar generate approximately 2 to 2.5%; Salary Saathi, 4 to 5%; and Mediclaim Financing, more than 7 to 8%

items.statement: Average borrowing cost reduced 163 bps YoY to 12.17% in Q4 FY2025-26; targets <10% in FY2026-27
items.quote: we are quite hopeful that our average cost of borrowing will further reduce to below 10% in FY2026-27

items.statement: AUM mix: Mediclaim 39%, EV/Solar 30%, Other Loans 29%, Salary Saathi 2% as of Mar 2026
items.quote: Across our four product lines today — Mediclaim Financing at 39%, Salary Saathi at 2%, EV and Solar at 30%, and Other Loans at 29%

items.statement: Mediclaim Financing disbursements target ₹1,500 crore in FY2026-27; industry premium >₹3 lakh crore growing 15%+ CAGR
items.quote: In FY2026-27, we ourselves are targeting ₹1,500 crore of disbursements in this segment alone

items.statement: Targets headcount reduction to ~300 in FY2026-27 from 420 in Q4 FY2025-26; disbursement/employee ₹4.21 cr
items.quote: Our target for FY2026-27 is to reduce headcount to approximately 300 people

items.statement: Raised ~₹300 crore equity in FY2025-26; plans PTC/DA transactions in FY2026-27 to avoid further equity dilution
items.quote: rather than diluting equity further, we will focus on PTC and DA transactions, which will improve our bottom line without requiring another equity raise

items.statement: CRISIL assigned 'A+ (SO)' rating to first Mediclaim securitization pool; Acuite upgraded rating to A- (Stable)
items.quote: We recently completed our first securitization pool rating for this product and received an 'A+ (SO)' rating from CRISIL

items.statement: FY27 outlook cautiously optimistic; demand resilient but monsoon (IMD 92% LPA, 82% El Nino probability) and fertilizer supply are key risks; planning assumes normal kharif and cost pass-through continues
items.quote: Overall, for FY '27, we are cautiously optimistic of the upcoming season based on the situations I described above.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin 42% (+107 bps), EBITDA margin 20.7% (+64 bps), net margin 16.8% (+68 bps) — all record highs; management targets sustainable margins via calibrated price hikes
items.quote: Our gross profit margin stands at 42% and our EBITDA margin stands at 20.7%. And also, our net profit margins are 16.8%. All record levels in the history of Sumitomo Chemical India.

items.statement: Cost pressures from rupee depreciation, raw materials, packaging, solvents, freight; 3 price hikes taken (15 Mar, 1 Apr, 1 May), more possible; calibrated product-by-product pass-through
items.quote: We have had, on 15th of March, a price increase, on 1st of April, a price increase, on 1st of May, a price increase, and now we will see whether we can increase the prices on 1st June.

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 4% YoY in FY26; branded formulation share rose to 81% from 79%; pure agro business grew 5-6% volume-driven; herbicides +19%, metal phosphates +11%; PGR/biostimulants hit by regulatory and weather
items.quote: Domestic revenue grew by 4% year-on-year in both Q4 and the full year, with the domestic franchise demonstrating genuine resilience.

items.statement: Specialty products 30% of domestic revenue; new products (past 3 years) contribute ~8% of domestic revenue; 7 launches in FY26 including Lentigo, Excalia Max; pipeline of 3-4 molecules from SCC for next 3-5 years
items.quote: These specialty products that have built our specialty business to 30% of our domestic revenues and it's these same new technologies where we will focus to build up the volume.

items.statement: INR150 cr Dahej project on track for commercialization in ~2 years; pipeline of similar-sized projects expected annually; additional techno-commercial feasibility underway; sustained capex pipeline over next decade
items.quote: First project we have announced at Dahej for INR150 crore, and then we are expecting a series of projects over next few years.

items.statement: Custom synthesis (CRAMS/CSM) revenue ~INR100-150 cr currently; expected to grow from FY28 as capex projects commercialize; parent co. elevated India to Tier-1 for early-stage molecule trials
items.quote: It is roughly in the range of INR100 crores to INR150 crores, depending upon the market situation in terms of volumes at this current level.

items.statement: Debt-free; cash & liquid investments INR2,113 cr (Mar'26); net worth INR3,394 cr (+17% YoY); RoCE 31%; capex to be funded from internal accruals; no external fund raise indicated
items.quote: Our cash and cash equivalents, including liquid investments as on 31st March 2026, were at approximately INR2,113 crores.

items.statement: Leadership transition: Chetan Shah to become Non-Executive Chairman from 1 Sep'26; Dr. Suresh Ramachandran elevated to MD; Sushil Marfatia retires; both to stay as advisors; Kunal Mittal, Hajime Shinomiya, Fumio Suzuki to anchor senior mana
items.quote: Dr. Suresh Ramachandran, who is currently serving as Deputy Managing Director, will be elevated to the position of Managing Director with effect from 1st September '26.

items.statement: Animal nutrition distribution restarted due to global supply chain issues; adds revenue at ~4-5% margin; not material to profitability; royalty arrangement for 2-3 products capped at INR2 cr annually
items.quote: Our company plans to restart distribution of these products immediately and we will continue distribution of these products for near future.

items.statement: Net working capital 103 days (vs 89 days) due to deliberate inventory buildup for kharif and tighter payables; receivables improved to 83 days; collections INR3,726 cr (+5%)
items.quote: Our net working capital stood at 103 days as of 31st March 2026 versus 89 days a year ago.

items.statement: FX exposure naturally hedged (exports ~imports ~USD70-80M each); no unhedged currency risk; rupee depreciation impact broadly neutral
items.quote: Our export and import are approximately equal in value, running at roughly USD 70 million to USD 80 million each on annual basis. As a result, the net foreign currency exposure of business is largely self-hedging.

items.statement: AGEasy exit monthly revenue run rate expected at INR14-16 crores this year.
items.quote: So, we expect that this should continue in this year as well, hoping that the exit monthly revenue run rate for this year should be somewhere in the range of INR14 crores to INR16 crores.

items.statement: Care Homes consolidated EBITDA breakeven expected in H1 FY28.
items.quote: So, since most of the beds came in the last 6 or 9 months, that breakeven on a consolidated basis for Care Homes is about FY28-ish.

items.statement: AGEasy EBITDA breakeven targeted by last quarter of this year.
items.quote: AGEasy by end of this year, last quarter, we should look at EBITDA breakeven. So, we are looking at that trajectory within this year.

items.statement: Path to profitability to be demonstrated in later part of FY27 for 1-2 verticals.
items.quote: So, we are hoping that 1 or 2 verticals will show that path to a later part of FY27. That's our intention.

items.statement: Remaining construction spend of INR70-75 crores for existing projects, mostly pending bills.
items.quote: We have approximately INR70 crores- INR75 crores of construction spend what we have to do. So, there are a lot of outstanding amounts, which are there to be paid and all that.

items.statement: E361 total management fee estimated at INR200 crores over project cycle.
items.quote: E361, we will have the total management fee of approximately INR200 crores. That is dependent on the price what we are seeing.

items.statement: E360 management fee estimated at INR130 crores since inception till project end.
items.quote: E360, we'll have a management fee of approximately INR130 crores since inception till the end of the project, end of the project sales cycle.

items.statement: Care Homes target ROCE 25-26% and EBITDA margin 18-20% at scale.
items.quote: The ROCE is expected to be in the range of 25%- 26% for Care Homes. And as per our model, which we have also discussed and shared with investors, at a post HO, all -inclusive costs, the Care Homes at scale should deliver an EBITDA of 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Care Home unit model: 4-6 quarters to breakeven at 40-45% occupancy; 8-10 quarters to 65-70% occupancy with 30%+ contribution margin and 16-18% EBITDA.
items.quote: a facility of 50 beds takes about 4 to 6 quarters to break even at about a 40%- 45% occupancy. And takes about 8 to 10 quarters to reach about 65%- 70%, when it starts producing a contribution margin at unit level of 30% plus and an EBITDA margin of 16% to 18%.

items.statement: Small price adjustments made due to higher COGS from China sourcing; no significant margin impact yet.
items.quote: However, for certain products, we have seen the COGS go up, and we've made small price adjustments to that effect as well.

items.statement: Noida Phase 2 market prices 2-3x last sale, expected INR16,000-18,000 per sq ft.
items.quote: No, the market, I said, is 2 to 3 times of what we sold last. So, the market is not INR27,000. The market will be around INR16,000 to INR18,000.

items.statement: AGEasy gross margins for online channels improved from 38% to 46% in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: Gross margins for D2C and marketplaces, the online channels improved from 38% at the start of the year to 46% in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Labour code impact of INR3-4 crores in FY27 P&L, mostly gratuity provisioning.
items.quote: On the labo ur code impact, it just came during March. So, this year, in FY27, we have accounted for it in our P&L. It's about INR3 crores to INR4 crores is the impact across all entities most of it is in gratuity provisioning, actually.

items.statement: Fundraise planned sometime this year, waiting for better market sentiment.
items.quote: But sometime this year, you will hear from us on what's happening on the fundraise side.

items.statement: Guides 15-20% revenue CAGR over next 5 years backed by Rs.18,000 crore order book, 2 AP WTE projects, and expanding EPR platform
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering 15% to 20% revenue CAGR over the next 5 years, backed by a record Rs.18,000 crores order book, 2 large-scale WTE projects in Andhra Pradesh and expanding EPR platform and India secured tailwind in urban-based infrastructure.

items.statement: Order book at all-time high of Rs.18,000 crores as of March 2026, split 60% processing and 40% C&T
items.quote: Our order book as of March 2026 stands at an all-time high of Rs.18,000 crores, providing exceptional revenue visibility, underpinning our confidence in sustained compounding growth ahead.

items.statement: Incremental capex of Rs.750 crores needed over 2-2.5 years for Atkoli processing, 2 AP WTE projects, and BMC C&T contracts
items.quote: The incremental capex would be the capex related to my processing contracts largely. So that's around Rs.750-odd crores of capex that I would need to invest to achieve this group.

items.statement: EBITDA margins held at ~22% for Q4 and full year FY26, in line with guidance; expects to maintain 20-22% margin profile
items.quote: EBITDA margins held at around 22% for both Q4 and for full year, in line with our stated guidance, reflecting disciplined cost management even as we invest in scale.

items.statement: 100% of revenue has escalation clauses; minimum wage hike impact only Rs.5.2 crores; escalations now recognized timely with elected municipal bodies in place
items.quote: All my projects, 100% of my revenue has escalation built into the system. So if minimum wage changes, as has been changed in the Labour Code that we have seen recently, it just had an implication of just Rs.5.2 crores for my entire books.

items.statement: C&D volumes doubled to 480-520 TPD from Feb 2026 due to BMC policy mandating authorized C&D processing; expects Rs.18-20 crore revenue in FY27
items.quote: We expect an uptick in the current year, from February onwards, the volumes have jumped. We are averaging around 480 to 520 tons per day as compared to 280 to 300 tons in the previous 8 months.

items.statement: Non-municipal revenue streams growing: RDF sales hit record 177,000 tons (+20% YoY), EPR credits monetized Rs.2.2 crore (potential 10% of PCMC WTE revenue), Click2Clean B2B segment launched
items.quote: Annual RDF sales reached a record 177,000 tons, up 20% year-on-year, further diversifying our non-municipal solid waste revenue base.

items.statement: Net debt/equity at 0.3x, gross debt Rs.426 crore, cash Rs.123 crore; A- rating at subsidiary, BBB+ at listed entity; cost of debt sub-10%; sufficient headroom for project financing
items.quote: Our net debt to equity stands at 0.3x, and the weighted average cost of debt is around 9.9%. The DSOs for the quarter was around 108 days.

items.statement: PCMC WTE plant operating at 86% PLF post-maintenance (vs 56% for FY26 due to 90 days shutdown); generated 69.3 MU green power, avoided 10,000 tons CO2e
items.quote: Post the maintenance period, our plant has been operating at approximately 86% PLF consistently.

items.statement: Targets INR 300 crores revenue in 3-4 years with 25-30% minimum EBITDA margin
items.quote: Over the next three to four years, I am targeting that we touch a number of about INR 300 crores, as a revenue without really losing the focus onto the profitability, which is around the same numbers, like between 25 -30% minimum as our EBITDA

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 232 crores with healthy pipeline of INR 436 crores
items.quote: As of today, our total order book stands at approximately INR 232 crores, while opportunity pipeline remains healthy at around INR 436 crores.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 24% from 23% in FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin also improved to 24% as compared to 23% in previous year.

items.statement: 60% of order book to convert to revenue this year, 40% of that recurring
items.quote: normally , our order book is consisting of about INR 200-odd crores. Out of the 60% will be booked almost this year in the revenue. And that 60%, I think, would be about 40% recurring revenue

items.statement: Pipeline conversion probability over 60%
items.quote: the probability level of conversions here are very high, more than about 60% is what I can close it with the numbers.

items.statement: DSO improved to 260 days from 372 days; cash collection cycle to 169 days from 270 days
items.quote: the company had improved its day sales outstanding. It was 372 days in FY25, which now improved to 260 days in FY26. Also, our cash collection cycle improved to 169 days from 270 days

items.statement: Targets INR 300 crore revenue in next three years (by FY29) with 50% from India and growing overseas share
items.quote: The revenue growth will come from a targeted growth of about INR 300 crores, which we are targeting in next three years

items.statement: Expects 25-27% revenue growth in FY27 over FY26 base of INR 133 crore
items.quote: We are expecting a growth rate of 25-27% in this year

items.statement: Conservative EBITDA margin target of 28-30% at INR 300 crore scale, with potential upside from high-margin TDR and overseas business
items.quote: So EBITDA on the conservative side, I would say we will always keep maintaining between 28-30%.

items.statement: TDR exchange business margins could reach 70-80% despite data center, maintenance, integration and support costs
items.quote: It could be touching about between 70-80%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue mix: CivitPERMIT ~50% (may increase), CivitINFRA ~25% (stable/slightly reduced), CivitBUILD/services 15-20%
items.quote: CivitPERMIT, would be higher side. So this year, CivitPERMIT was 50% of our total revenue, and we expect the same percentage in next FY27 as well.

items.statement: TDR exchange mandatory from May 10 at BMC with INR 8,000 crore annual transaction volume; expanding to MMRDA, Navi Mumbai, Thane, Vasai-Virar
items.quote: This is currently at BMC, but we are working with multiple other municipalities in Mumbai and MMRD zones.

items.statement: TDR revenue model: 0.5% fee on each transaction volume on the exchange
items.quote: This is purely a transaction model. This is we get 0.5% of the transactions made on TDR exchange.

items.statement: Intangible assets (INR 70 cr) and intangible under development (INR 19 cr) reflect product R&D capitalized and amortized over 3-4 years
items.quote: We have a very strong amortization schemes, of course, like basically once the product is capitalized, we depreciate amortizing within three years or four years kind of period.

items.statement: Government receivables remain a challenge; trade receivables INR 34 crore vs INR 120 crore revenue; improving via transaction/recurring revenue models
items.quote: Trade receivables, though, of course, as we said, we move more and more towards quality revenues through transaction based model or recurring revenues based model, it will keep going down.

items.statement: Germany traction expected in Q3-Q4 FY27; US small orders ongoing targeting larger deals; Middle East traction starting
items.quote: Germany is something where we are actually very passionately working on, and we are definitely looking forward to good news in maybe Q3 of this year and Q4 of this year.

items.statement: Team of ~550 people (70%+ R&D/implementation, 25-30 business development); aims to grow revenue faster than headcount via AI/automation
items.quote: We are a total team of about 550 people. And out of which like the research, development, implementation of this all includes about 70% more than that.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin increase of 1-2% in FY27 over current levels
items.quote: Within this financial year, we target that like the EBITDA margin that we are currently enjoying, overall, it should go up by at least 1% to 2%.

items.statement: Expect 20% volume growth from new capacity of 9,000-10,000 tons annually starting September 2026
items.quote: So, their increased capacity would be annually around 9,000 tons to 10,000 tons. Okay? So you can say around say, 20% of the growth is expected from the enhanced volumes.

items.statement: Target 85% capacity utilization at consolidated facility by August-September 2026
items.quote: I expect that the current facility from, say, August or September onwards, once the entire shifting and consolidation is over, should reach around 85% level

items.statement: New 4-acre integrated facility at Modinagar expected operational very soon; unit 2 shifting already underway
items.quote: And the good news is that as we speak over this earnings call, we expect the new unit to be operational very soon, and already unit second shifting is going on effectively to the new facility and the new facility is very much ready to move.

items.statement: GI wire margins expected at 20-25%, significantly higher than current product mix
items.quote: It would be around easily around 20%. 20% to 25%.

items.statement: High-margin products (pneumatic nails, stainless steel bars, alloy steel bars) contribution increased from January 2026
items.quote: For the last 5 months, let's say from January 2026, the products whose sales we have increased are all high-value, high-margin kind of products that is pneumatic nails, stainless steel bars and alloy steel bars.

items.statement: Export order book currently at highest level in company history
items.quote: I think today, our export order book would be the highest in the history as on date currently.

items.statement: Dubai warehousing subsidiary delayed due to geopolitical conflict; will resume when situation stabilizes
items.quote: Creating a subsidiary of Maiden Forgings Limited, 100% owned subsidy in Gulf, UAE particularly. I was there in Dubai. We also initiated the process from 9th February to 15th February, I believe. Then this war broke out, so we had to hold on for a moment. We are waiting for the war to subside.

items.statement: LOIs secured from existing customers for new GI wire and stainless steel component product lines
items.quote: We already have the LOIs from the existing customer itself. We don't require any additional marketing cost for them or marketing efforts for them as on date. So, we already have the LOIs from the customer for both the product lines.

items.statement: Target 20-25% of sales from B2G/defense segment in medium term
items.quote: I expect. I target not expect that 20% to 25% of our sales should come from the B2G segment in the mid-term future.

items.statement: All FY26 growth and capex funded through internal accruals; no external capital raised
items.quote: No external capital has been raised during the financial year from any financial institution or in form of equity for this entire capex as well as the growth in the top line. Entire growth and capex has been funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: H2 FY26 margin improvement driven primarily by product mix change, not raw material price movements
items.quote: No, no, no. majorly due to product mix.

items.statement: Pneumatic nails facility utilization at 60-70% as of April 2026
items.quote: If I talk about -- if I talk about the last month or last to last month, like from April onwards or March onwards, maybe, we are utilizing it at 60% to 70% level now, the pneumatic nails.

items.statement: Plan to migrate from BSE SME to main board; all criteria fulfilled, transition at appropriate time
items.quote: We have also made the company prepared for the switch to main board from the SME, fulfilling all the criteria required for the switch. And at the right time, we would be making this transition.

items.statement: Management expects to grow ahead of industry in FY27 but avoids formal revenue/EBITDA guidance; will provide indication at Q1 earnings call
items.quote: We believe we will continue to be ahead of the India pack, and that's really all I can say. I don't want to give you formal guidance right now, Mehul. But at the end of our Q1 call, we will have much clearer visibility in terms of where we are headed.

items.statement: FY27 revenue visibility at 85-90% from existing contracts, balance 10% to be built during the year
items.quote: So we have visibility of between 85% and 90%. The balance 10% or thereabouts, we'll have to find.

items.statement: Cash of INR450 crores to be deployed across acquisitions (primary), organic growth (AI, technology, talent), and shareholder rewards (dividend or buyback)
items.quote: Acquisitions, of course, remain the primary use of this cash. At the same time, the Board will consider options to also reward loyal shareholders in the future and to invest for internal organic growth.

items.statement: IFM EBITDA margin at 4.5% for FY26; BSS adjusted EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin at 5.9%
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA after taking this onetime loss due to Avon incident for the year stood at INR176 crores with the adjusted EBITDA margin standing at 5.9%.

items.statement: Denave Q4 EBITDA margin improved to 5.5%+ with 70% EBITDA growth; Athena margins stabilized at 19-20%; Matrix margins stable at 11-12%
items.quote: During the quarter, revenue at Denave grew 15% and EBITDA grew almost 70% with margin improvement to 5.5% plus for Q4.

items.statement: IFM seeing strong traction across manufacturing, commercial real estate, healthcare, retail, logistics and GCC-led demand; added 30 new logos in FY26
items.quote: During the year, we added 30 new logos across industrial, technology, commercial sectors, while also witnessing increased wallet share from existing clients.

items.statement: Healthcare now contributes 7.8% of revenue; IFM segment 67% of total revenue; BSS segment 33%
items.quote: The year saw a meaningful increase in contribution from health care, which reflects our deliberate effort to diversify our industry exposure. It now contributes about 7.8% of our revenue.

items.statement: Avon logistics/freight brokerage provision of INR23 crores fully provided; core Avon business grew 9% and remains stable; no recurrence expected
items.quote: Over the last two quarters, Avon took a total provision of approximately INR23 crores relating to receivables from its relatively new logistics and freight brokerage business.

items.statement: Wage code impact of INR5 crores at group level and INR4 crores at UDS standalone taken in FY26; not expected to repeat
items.quote: There is also a INR4 crores hit that we have taken at UDS level and overall a INR5 crores number on the wage code liabilities that we have taken on board.

items.statement: Denave revenue INR590 crores (EBITDA INR26 crores), Athena INR116.8 crores (EBITDA INR24 crores), Matrix INR128.6 crores (EBITDA INR15 crores) for FY26
items.quote: Denave revenue was at INR590 crores. Athena revenue was at INR116.8 crores. Matrix revenue was at INR128.6 crores. Overall BSS was at INR968 crores.

items.statement: Acquisition deal still on; due diligence almost closed but other negotiating items ongoing; cannot guarantee closure but cautiously hopeful
items.quote: The conversations have taken longer than what we had envisaged. The DD is almost closed, but there are other negotiating items that are right now being done.

items.statement: IFM strategic priorities for FY27: improve client-level profitability, technology-led efficiency, optimize manpower deployment, expand higher-margin specialized services (energy management, MEP, technical AMC)
items.quote: Our strategic priorities for IFM in FY '27 remains focused on improving client level profitability across the portfolio, increasing operational efficiency through technology -led interventions, optimizing manpower deployment to improve margin quality.

items.statement: Denave onboarded 49 new logos in FY26; new business from existing enterprise customers grew 21% YoY; signed at higher margins with favorable service mix
items.quote: During the year, we almost onboarded 49 new logos and also added new business from our existing debt enterprise customers as well. And both put together grew 21% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Writing instruments revenue target INR500+ crores in FY27 vs INR368 crores in FY26
items.quote: Overall, what we expect from the writing instrument category is a INRS500 crores plus next year kind of revenmie, which currently stood at about INR368 crores for this year.

items.statement: Consumerware EBITDA margin improvement of 2.5-3% expected in FY27 as steel ware ramps and glassware turns profitable
items.quote: Steel ware as it ramps up and glassware as it starts becoming more profitable, we should sce improvement about 2.5%, 3% EBITDA margins in the consumerware category.

items.statement: MRP hikes of 12-20% taken across all product lines to pass on rising raw material and production costs
items.quote: There has been a lot of escalation in prices, about 12% to 20% MRP rises that we have taken across all our product lincs, which we had to because of these rising costs.

items.statement: Glassware at 60% utilization, breakeven; peak revenue INR300 crores with 28-30% EBITDA margin at optimal utilization
items.value: INR300 crores peak revenue; 28-30% EBITDA margin
items.quote: I think we're looking at about INR300 crores of peak revenue from glassware and our peak would be about 28% to 30% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Capacity expansion to 16,000 machines/year on track for commercial operations in Q2 FY27 (September 2026)
items.quote: Our plan to expand our annual capacity to 16,000 machines remain on track for a commencement of commercial operation in quarter 2 of this financial year.

items.statement: Outstanding order book at INR 4,732 crores as of March 31, 2026, diversified across sectors
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, our outstanding order book stand at INR4,732 crores, which is very healthy and growing.

items.statement: Raw material costs up 2-3% in last 2 months; prices increased for new orders from May 1, 2026 to offset
items.quote: Today, in the last 2 months, we have seen the cost has been increased, close to 2 to 3 percentage over there on raw material prices. On our -- from 1st of this May, we have increased our prices for the new -- to our new customers and new orders over there basically.

items.statement: Strong demand across aerospace, defense, auto, general engineering; inquiries converting to orders at fastest pace
items.quote: The outlook across both domestic and global markets remain positive across all manufacturing sectors and especially we have seen a good pickup in auto and general engineering sectors.

items.statement: FY26 order intake: 27% aerospace, 28% auto, 31% general engineering; order book: 38% aerospace, 20% auto, 19% general engineering, 4% EMS
items.quote: For FY26, the order intake stood at INR2364 crores. This includes 27% of aerospace, 28% of auto and auto component and 31% from general engineering.

items.statement: Export control investigation at Huron ongoing; INR 67 crore revenue deferred (not written off); no material operational impact; timeline uncertain
items.quote: An ongoing investigation is being conducted by the export control authorities concerning certain export order at Huron. The investigation has had no material adverse impact on the company's operations, including order execution, exports, customer servicing or ongoing manufacturing activities.

items.statement: INR 300 crores debt incurred for capacity expansion in FY26; working capital debt up only INR 45 crores; expect cash flow improvement post-expansion
items.quote: Close to INR300 crores is the debt has been incurred on our capacity expansion basically, okay, on our new capacity there. Only working capital has increased only INR45 crores to be there.

items.statement: EMS segment orders delayed as customers optimizing capacity; no major investment in last 1.5 years; PLI scheme expansion may drive future orders
items.quote: Right now, they all are optimizing their manufacturing capabilities and capacity there. So we are just -- the delay side we are seeing from all the EMS player there. Nothing has been invested much on the last component manufacturing in the last 1.5 years there.

items.statement: Targeting 25%+ EBITDA margin steady state regardless of mix shift; average realization may decline to INR 30 lakh at full 16,000 capacity but margins sustained
items.quote: Even let's say we see that in a forward situation, okay, in our -- this additional INR6,000 to INR16,000, if we reach to a full -- let's say, full utilization, even the margin -- let's say, the machine average price will reach to INR30 lakhs. Still we'll be at around at close to 25%. It will not go down there.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected to be better than Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY26 on both GTV and GP, assuming status quo on geopolitics
items.quote: We would expect to see both the YoY growth from Q1 of last year as well as QoQ growth from Q4 of last year.

items.statement: Aspiration to grow GP in early-to-mid 20s percentage range for FY27 unless serious downward movement in base normalcy
items.quote: The whole business plan was anchored around this growing north of 20%. We do believe that unless some serious downward movement happens in the base of where normalcy sets in, we should continue to grow in that range.

items.statement: EBITDA-to-GTV ratio expected to move up in FY27 as SG&A growth tapers and higher-margin hotels business grows faster than air GTV
items.quote: I think that's a reasonable assumption and it's a function of two things. One yes, absolutely as SG&A growth tapers down margins should expand and secondly the saliency mix will also help as our hotels business, which is higher margin business grows faster than the air GTV.

items.statement: Classic Vacations integration halfway through, targeting completion by end of Q3 FY27 (end of calendar year 2026)
items.quote: We are probably about halfway through the integration process, but we intend to complete the integration by the end of Q3, by the end of this Calendar Year.

items.statement: Debt repayment moratorium for one year; repayments start Q3 FY27 and continue for four years per current agreement
items.quote: We have a debt for a period of five years. So, we have a moratorium on repayment for one year. A repayment would start from Q3 of this year and would be, would remain there for another four years.

items.statement: Targeting >100% CFO-to-EBITDA and FCF-to-EBITDA conversion by end of FY27 as timing issues (Brazil, war-related receivables) resolve
items.quote: Historically, as well, we have been delivering more than 100% per se and that's what we would strive to do by end of this financial year as well.

items.statement: LATAM (Brazil) to see moderate growth in FY27 due to currency volatility, IOF tax, and structural headwinds beyond company control
items.quote: LATAM will see moderate growth compared to the overall enterprise because of the fact that there are significant headwinds which go beyond just our own business over there.

items.statement: Expects to maintain FY25-26 performance levels, with review after Q2 if conditions improve.
items.quote: But we expect we'll at least we will maintain FY25-'26 levels of performance as of now.

items.statement: Targets minimum 10% margin, with operational efficiency aiming for 10-13% acceptable level.
items.quote: 10% to 13% will be an acceptable margin level what we are foreseeing.

items.statement: No major capex planned this year; focus on automation and AI for cost reduction.
items.quote: There is no much capex planned this year.

items.statement: UAE plant capacity 1,200 metric tons, utilization less than 50%, expects gradual improvement.
items.quote: Our capacity is 1,200 metric tons in the Ras Al Khaimah plant. And currently, less than 50% is being utilized in this Ras Al Khaimah plant.

items.statement: UAE market down due to geopolitical issues; hopeful recovery by end of next quarter.
items.quote: In the last quarter, from the last quarter onwards, due to all these geopolitical issues and all, the market is totally down in the GCC area.

items.statement: GST revision reduced new tyre rates, pressuring retread margins; association seeking 5% GST for retread.
items.quote: So due to this there is a pressure on the retread business margin, margin of the retread business.

items.statement: Expanding product portfolio with heavy-duty tractor rear tyres, receiving encouraging market response.
items.quote: The newly introduced heavy-duty tractor rear tyre category has started receiving encouraging response from the market through our dealer network and further strengthens our position in the agriculture segment.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties and war in Middle East causing market volatility and delayed purchases.
items.quote: But due to a lot of other factors, we could do at least 12%. That is the growth what we could attain.

items.statement: Terra Rubber recycling initiative expected to improve material efficiency and margins over time.
items.quote: This initiative is expected to improve material utilization efficiencies and strengthen operating margins over time.

items.statement: Expanded Western India presence with new depot in Gujarat, operational from December 1, 2025.
items.quote: In line with our strategy to strengthen domestic distribution and improve customer reach, we also expanded our presence in Western India through the launch of a new depot in Gujarat, which commenced operations on December 1st, 2025.

items.statement: UAE operations margins better than India operations.
items.quote: The margins are better than India operations.

items.statement: Working capital increased due to extended credit period and high inventory; plans to reduce gradually.
items.quote: Gradually the overall plan is to reduce this to a comfortable level in another few quarters.

items.statement: Exploring inorganic growth opportunities in recycling under Terra Rubber.
items.quote: And going forward, we are looking at some acquisitions in of some facility in this area. That is what we have in mind in Terra Rubber.

items.statement: Total order book at INR6,814 crores, providing revenue visibility for 24 months.
items.quote: On the order book and execution front, our total order book has surged to over INR6,814 crores, providing robust revenue visibility over the next 24 months.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow guidance of at least INR2,500 crores.
items.quote: For FY27, we would look forward to at least INR2,500 crores further order book.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected to be INR20-30 crores, not more.
items.quote: So we don't see any major capex going on. Apart from the capex which we have done in the last financial year, but I think it can be to the tune of INR20 crores, INR30-odd crores, not more than that.

items.statement: BESS EPC projects expected to have PAT margin around 10%.
items.quote: In the BESS business, which is EPC, we will expect PAT margin somewhere in the range of 10%.

items.statement: Renewable segment blended PAT margin expected 10-12%.
items.quote: Likewise, I confirmed in the BESS segment, at present the margin range seems to be somewhere around 10%, and we look forward to achieving PAT margins in the range of 10% to 12%, a blended one from the renewables.

items.statement: Price variation clauses partially offset cost increases, but not fully.
items.quote: In maximum of the contracts, it is a price variation clause which is applicable. So a part of the cost increase will definitely get offset with the price variation clause. However, it does not take into account the entire price increase in the market.

items.statement: Bid pipeline: INR1,200 crores submitted, INR5,000 crores upcoming.
items.quote: Current bid pipeline as of now is somewhere around -- the bid pipeline where we have submitted our bid is somewhere around INR1,200 crores, and the projects for which bidding is to happen where we are interested, it is somewhere around INR5,000 crores further.

items.statement: FY27 revenue split: INR1,350 crores from water/wastewater, INR650 crores from renewables.
items.quote: On the whole, if I say INR2,000 crores is the visibility, somewhere around INR1,350 crores is what we are expecting from the water and wastewater treatment sector and INR650 crores is what we look forward to as the topline from the Renewable segment.

items.statement: Global crisis may cause 1-2% EBITDA margin pressure.
items.quote: There is one geopolitical global crisis which has happened, due to which some costs have also gone for a rise. So there will be a pressure, maybe to an extent of 1 to 2 percentage points.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected to reduce to around 90 days in FY27.
items.quote: Definitely. For me, as we understand, the working capital cycle should come down to somewhere around 90 days, which is a prudent working capital cycle.

items.statement: Debt level at 0.34, maximum 1:1 debt-to-equity targeted.
items.quote: The present debt level is 0.34. We do understand that maximum, and if I talk about all the extremes, a 1:1 debt level is we would not like to cross at any point of time.

items.statement: Three-year plan aims to achieve INR200 crores topline while maintaining and improving current EBITDA margin
items.quote: So sir, our initial -- like our top -- our goal as our intention for the next three years is to achieve INR200 crores top line maintaining the current EBITDA margin and improving it.

items.statement: Epitome Cloud acquisition for INR40 crores total consideration, funded via IPO proceeds and internal accruals without external debt
items.quote: Importantly, this transaction is expected to be funded through IPO proceeds and balance will be funded through internal accruals available without external debt.

items.statement: Nine international trade shows in FY26 generated over 500 qualified leads and multiple enterprise opportunities under active discussion
items.quote: These initiatives generated over 500 qualified leads and multiple enterprise opportunities currently under active discussion.

items.statement: Management expects 200 basis point EBITDA margin improvement in FY27 driven by operating leverage, productivity gains, improved utilization, and higher-value enterprise engagements
items.quote: The expected improvement is driven by operating leverage from Gurgaon expansion, productivity gains from recent senior hires, improved utilizations, and expected contribution from higher -value enterprise engagements.

items.statement: AI projects start as fixed-cost discovery/POC engagements then transition to T&M model for production deployments
items.quote: So all AI contracts basically start as a discovery, which is a fixed cost agreement. So we charge a certain fee upfront for exploring business case and demand creating a POC for them. As soon as it transitions to production, it becomes a T&M contract where we basically deploy teams, which is billed on a monthly contrac

items.statement: No buyback planned; capital allocated to acquisitions (2-3 more targeted) and organic growth investments including US office expansion
items.quote: Right now, we have not considered any buyback. So, we plan to utilize our capital towards growth and expansion. So, we are being more aggressive on the acquisition and business development side.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with INR171.3 crores total cash and investments; current ratio ~29.8x; operating cash generation INR17.29 crores in FY26
items.quote: This resulted in a total cash and investment of approximately INR171.3 crores. The company remains fully debt -free with substantial financial flexibility and liquidity.

items.statement: Interim dividend of 10% face value paid in FY26; final dividend of 10% face value proposed subject to AGM approval; total payout ~20-25% of profit
items.quote: During financial year 26, the company distributed an interim dividend of 10% of face value. Additionally, the board has approved a proposed final dividend of 10% of face value, subject to shareholder approval at the forthcoming Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Epitome Cloud acquisition expected to close within 8-12 weeks; due diligence completed, definitive agreement discussions in advanced stages
items.quote: So the due diligence has been completed. We are in the process of signing the definitive agreement. We expect it to complete within 8 to 12 weeks.

items.statement: Targets over 125,000 units in FY27, with 75-80% YoY revenue growth.
items.quote: We are targeting more than 125,000 units scale for this year. I am committed to sustaining 75% to 80% year-on-year revenue growth as our structural trajectory.

items.statement: Plans to expand dealer network to over 550 dealers in FY27.
items.quote: Currently, we have more than 400 dealers. And this year, we are planning to expand it to more than 550 dealers.

items.statement: Aims to maintain profitability and margins despite expansion and branding spend.
items.quote: However much we expand, however much budget we keep, our focus is to keep profitability and margins similar. We have no intention to reduce, deduct, or decrease them for branding and promotions.

items.statement: Average selling price expected to rise from INR45,000 to INR50,000.
items.quote: It will go from INR45,000 to INR50,000, sir, in the upcoming time.

items.statement: Plans 5-6 models with 70-80% local content by 2027.
items.quote: By 2027, I clear this to you, we will have five to six vehicles which will be properly 70%, 80% will be Make in India.

items.statement: Expects low-speed EV market to grow 20-25% annually.
items.quote: And it is sure that the market will grow 20%-25%.

items.statement: Plans to move to quarterly reporting in future.
items.quote: In the future, we will surely move to quarterly reporting, but it will take some time.

items.statement: Marketing spend expected over INR1-2 crores this year, excluding IPL.
items.quote: This year, sir, more than INR1 crore, INR1 crores to INR2 crores after IPL expenses.

items.statement: Aims to capture over 20-30% EV market share within 2-3 years.
items.quote: And sir, let me clear this, not in 5-10 years, but within 2 to 3 years, we will acquire more than 20%-30% of the EV market.

items.statement: Targeting 70-80% revenue growth for FY27 while improving profitability and operating leverage
items.quote: Based on the visibility across our existing operations and upcoming growth initiatives, we are targeting revenue growth of 70 -80% for FY27, while continuing to improve profitability and operating leverage across the platform.

items.statement: Expect Meevaa Foods to contribute 15-20% of overall revenues in FY27
items.quote: We expect Meevaa Foods to contribute about 15-20% of overall revenues in FY27, while also strengthening our presence in higher -margin and value -added two categories.

items.statement: Anticipate approximately 25% improvement in overall margin profile driven by Meevaa and seafood integration
items.quote: There will be an increase, in my view, approximately 25%, overall, on the margin profile.

items.statement: Targeting 3-4% EBITDA margin improvement over next two years from aquaculture, ready-to-eat expansion, and B2C mix shift
items.quote: Over the next two years, we are targeting an improvement of 3-4% at least in the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: B2B/B2C revenue split to stabilize at 50-50% from current 68%/32%
items.quote: We feel that B2B and B2C at the steady number, at a going forward will be around 50-50 as a number broadly.

items.statement: Fish and seafood contribution to rise from 27% to 30-35% of revenue in FY27
items.quote: Fish and seafood is already currently at 27% of contribution, which will move to at least 30 -35%.

items.statement: Scaling partner store network from 100 to 300-400 stores by year-end; each store averages INR 5 lakh monthly revenue at 8-10% net margin
items.quote: We have already identified and onboarded approximately 100 stores and are targeting to scale this network to nearly 300 -400 partner stores by year end.

items.statement: Biggest execution risk cited as macroeconomic factors including war, export shipping, and raw material pressures
items.quote: Biggest execution risk. I think, we are looking at from a macroeconomic point of view, I think the war as a factor is a risk for our business, because we're now looking at exports and shipping outside the country, some raw material pressures.

items.statement: Value-added/frozen products expected to reach 20-25% of total revenue over next 3-5 years
items.quote: Overall, in the scheme of things, it should be approximately 20% - 25% minimum of the total revenue, which is a good number.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit top line growth in FY27
items.quote: We remain focused on the larger opportunity ahead and are targeting double-digit top line growth in FY27.

items.statement: DG Sets business organic growth target 11-12% in FY27
items.quote: So we target an organic growth of about 11%, 12%. So as I was saying, addressing sir's question, we expect organic growth at about 11% to 12% from our DG space.

items.statement: Additional 50 MW wind capex planned in FY27 with higher depreciation
items.quote: So in FY27, you might see some higher in terms of depreciation as we capitalize 50 megawatts, whether we are going to capitalize another 50 megawatt during the year.

items.statement: Wind EPC order pipeline of 585 MW executable till December 2027
items.quote: Ma'am, we already have an order pipeline of almost, you can say, 585 -megawatt order, which we are executing. So till December '27, we have enough orders.

items.statement: Data center DG order book visibility 9 months to 1 year
items.quote: We have a strong order book of nine months work -- 9 months to about a year of work cut out ahead of us.

items.statement: FY27 margins expected to improve from Q2 as wind generation rises and 50 MW IPP adds revenue
items.quote: And for '27, we believe we will be in the target. But going forward, on the subsequent quarter, this will be materially clear and we'll come back. Further, the margin -- overall margin, if you see from a business side, it is a Genset as well as on the wind side. And as our 50 -megawatt installation that the revenue gen

items.statement: Wind IPP EBITDA margin 87-88% first year, stabilizing at 82-83%
items.quote: The new projects, the first year of the operation, it will be around 88% - 87% of the EBITDA. And gradually, after -- once the operation maintenance will start, it will stabilize at 82% - 83% of the EBITDA margin in the IPP.

items.statement: Finance cost to reduce substantially in Q1 FY27 after INR525 cr debt repayment post-IPO
items.quote: Following our IPO, the company has repaid the existing debt of INR525 crores in quarter 1 2027. And currently, company holds a cash, including investment of approximately INR450 crores as on May 26. And as a result of substantial reduction is expected in the finance cost in Q1 FY27, and that is directly going to enhanc

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties weighing on near-term demand especially Q1 FY27
items.quote: Geopolitical uncertainties, rising energy prices and supply chain pressures are beginning to weigh on near -term demand, especially in Q1 FY2 7.

items.statement: Data center demand surging post-budget with robust inquiry pipeline
items.quote: Post budget announcement, there are even surge in the inquiry that's coming in and a lot of the people are to install a data center. So we see very robust order book is very strong. Also, the inquiry is very strong that is coming in.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting to 75-80% DG Sets and 20-25% Wind by FY27 from 83-17% in FY26
items.quote: You might see from a revenue side, it will be ranging between 75% to 80% on the Gen set and 20% to 25% ranges that will come into the wind vis -a-vis the EBITDA side, you will see the shift.

items.statement: Wind project land acquisition and ROW challenges persist for Khavda 2 GW RE park
items.quote: As far as Khavda project is concerned, it's a long -term project along with the joint venture with GE Vernova. And still we are in the process of getting the land from the Gujarat government. Post getting the land from the Gujarat government, only this project will get initiated with the IPP customers. So till now, the

items.statement: Platino RECD Q4 FY26 sales INR22 cr, PBT INR5.8 cr; expects acceleration from state mandates
items.quote: So the Platino has a INR22 crores of sales with INR5.8 crores of PBT during the quarter -- Q4 of FY26.

items.statement: Expect AUM growth north of 40% in FY27 with disciplined asset quality and strong secured business scale-up
items.quote: We expect to grow at north of 40% in AUM, with disciplined asset quality and calibrated risk selection, while secured business scale-up is also expected to be strong.

items.statement: Target gross NPA below 2.25% and 10-15% year-on-year reduction in impairment costs for FY27
items.quote: On asset quality, we are targeting gross NPA below 2.25%, year-on-year reduction in impairment costs of 10%-15%, and continued improvement in Stage-1 mix.

items.statement: Target return on average AUM of 4.5-5% and return on average equity of 19-21% for FY27
items.quote: On profitability, we are targeting a return on average AUM in the range of 4.5%-5%, which entails a return on average equity in the range of 19-21%.

items.statement: Plan to add at least 80 LAP branches by end of FY27, reaching ~178 total branches
items.quote: On the LAP business, today, we have 98 branches. We plan to have at least 80 more branches by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Portfolio yield moderated to ~30-31% in Q4 FY26 from ~30.5-31.75% in Q3; expect continued yield compression over next 4-6 quarters
items.quote: Our portfolio yield is close to about 30 or 31% in Q4. And you asked about last quarter, the last quarter may have been higher by, I would say, 50 to 75 basis points.

items.statement: Expect average spread (yield minus cost of borrowing) of 18-19% near term, reducing to 14-16% over 3-4 quarters
items.quote: Yield minus the cost of borrowing will basically be closer to about 18 to 19% in the near term and in the longer term, it will be, it will reduce, like I said, yes.

items.statement: Deliberately reducing rates to attract higher-quality customers; passing on operating leverage and funding cost benefits
items.quote: The moderation and margins are substantially linked to a very calibrated shift towards high quality customer segments, which of course is priced lower, but they also exhibit a very superior long-term credit behavior.

items.statement: April-May disbursement momentum continues strong; 3.5M active customers and 11.76M unique customers provide repeat demand visibility
items.quote: The short answer to your second question is Yes, the same momentum is visible.

items.statement: ₹630 crore (75% of IPO proceeds) infused into NBFC subsidiary Si Creva; balance 25% deployed for tech, AI, brand, acquisition
items.quote: On the IPO proceeds, 75% of the primary issue, approximately ₹ 630 crore have been already infused as fresh equity into our NBFC subsidiary, which is Si Creva Capital.

items.statement: Created wholly-owned subsidiary for mutual fund and wealth product distribution as part of non-lending expansion strategy
items.quote: Now, it so happens if you have to distribute mutual fund, it is best done via separate entity and that is why we have created this fully-owned subsidiary for selling mutual fund and other wealth products primarily.

items.statement: Engineering order book at INR 26,433 million as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: As at 31st March '26, the engineering order book stood at INR 26,433 million, providing healthy revenue visibility going forward.

items.statement: Oman DBOOT project CAPEX of USD 40 million over next two years funded by debt and equity
items.quote: The CAPEX is around USD 40 million over the next two years, and we'll be funding it with a mix of debt and equity.

items.statement: FY27 maintenance and routine CAPEX estimated at Rs 30-40 crores; no major expansion planned yet
items.quote: At this juncture, the CAPEX what we have envisaged is more into the maintenance and routine CAPEX, which is in the region of around Rs.30 to 40 crores.

items.statement: Roha plant targeting 25% capacity utilization in first full year of operation (FY27)
items.quote: Our guidance has been in the past that we will work towards 25% capacity utilization of the Roha plant in the first full year of operation.

items.statement: Sri Lanka project expected to complete by end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: The closure of the Sri Lanka project continues to progress as planned and we expect to complete the project by the end of the 2nd Quarter of the Financial Year 2027.

items.statement: Legacy engineering project expected to close in FY27
items.quote: We should be able to close it in this financial year. The guidance we can offer is that just to close out in this financial year.

items.statement: Chemical segment EBIT margin impact: Roha depreciation/interest ~7% in Q4, ~3% for full year; input cost and logistics ~1% in Q4
items.quote: The Roha impact will be just under 7% for the quarter and what Mr. Indraneel was explaining was the overall impact for the full year.

items.statement: Engineering segment margin hit by Rs 60 crore export deferral to GCC due to West Asia crisis
items.quote: On engineering margins, we faced headwinds due to deferral of certain export shipments—approximately Rs. 60 crore—related to the West Asia crisis.

items.statement: Initiated pricing actions to pass on input cost increases (styrene, oleum) to chemical customers
items.quote: We have initiated appropriate pricing action to pass on the cost increases to the customers.

items.statement: Engineering order intake 40% higher than last full financial year; majority expected to execute in FY27 and FY28
items.quote: Apart from that, our order intake has been quite healthy; in fact, it has been 40% more than the last full financial year, and we expect a majority of those projects to get executed in this financial year and the next.

items.statement: MANN+HUMMEL partnership for UF PVDF flat sheet membranes and MBR technology to strengthen membrane portfolio
items.quote: This partnership with MANN+HUMMEL was made with the intention of further expanding the membrane portfolio to have the latest technologies of ultra-filtration PVDF-type flat sheet membranes and to get the MBR technology.

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing logistics disruption, higher raw material costs (styrene, oleum), and export deferrals impacting Q4 and continuing into Q1 FY27
items.quote: The crisis is ongoing, and we expect the impact to continue into this quarter until logistics and shipping lines resume normal operations.

items.statement: Expects positive demand momentum to sustain in FY27 with improving caustic soda realizations QoQ
items.quote: Looking ahead to financial year 2027, we are optimistic about the demand environment.
